+# S06 — Energy/control operation under hidden pathways
+
+15 October 2026, Australia/Brisbane. **Candidate status: unbuilt; full-system net output and advantage UNKNOWN.** The strongest operation I can specify is a **thermally self-clocked, two-bank pyroelectric heat engine**: a thermal relay alternates each bank's contact with a metered hot stream and cold sink, while an electrical recovery circuit runs the charge cycle and delivers DC to a storage bus. The relay is a physical temperature measurement and actuator paid by the same heat flow. It does not require microscopic knowledge of domain switching or heat pathways; it does require measured *terminal* polarization loops, thermal response, leakage, relay thresholds and the complete energy ledger. The existing literature already contains watt-scale actively cycled pyroelectric output and microwatt passive-contact cycling. Combining them has no demonstrated positive net power or novelty-cleared advantage.
+
+## Service and physical assembly
+
+The useful service is sustained **net DC electricity at a specified bus voltage**, supplied from a declared hot stream and cold sink. A fair demonstration would fix their inlet temperatures, flow/pressure budgets, contact footprint, mass, and lifetime, then meter hot and cold enthalpy flows and every electrical input/output. The target of 1 W-class net DC is a *design target*, motivated by an existing 1 W generator report, not a prediction for this assembly.
+
+Two characterized ferroelectric multilayer-capacitor banks (A and B) operate in antiphase. A thermally attached bistable strip or bellows changes over two thermal contacts/valves when its local temperature crosses upper/lower thresholds. An electrical contact on the same relay can request the high/low field transitions, but phase lag and electrocaloric kicks must be measured. An inductor and switches transfer rather than dissipate most of the large field energy between the two banks. A rectifier/converter delivers the remaining net electrical energy to storage. A finite thermal regenerator between the banks can exchange some sensible heat before each contacts its reservoir. The relay and the charge-transfer circuit are not free: their motion, leakage, switching, startup charge, calibration and standby draw are in the system ledger.
+
+This co-design is meant to reduce active sensing and timing dependence under drift. The bimetallic relay responds to an actual thermal state, while the electrical port supplies a direct measure of cycle work. It cannot infer unobserved heat leakage, pump power or fatigue. Its alleged advantage is therefore lower complete-system overhead or greater reliability than active control, **not** a new source of work. A precharged capacitor is startup inventory; sustained output must be shown after many cycles with its stored energy nondecreasing or explicitly deducted.
+
+## Derived operating conditions (original calculation)
+
+Let the bank plus attached relay have measured thermal capacitance (C), intended contact conductance (G), off-state parasitic conductance (G_\ell), hot/cold reservoirs (T_H>T_C), and relay thresholds (T_\downarrow<T_\uparrow). A first thermal-port model gives
+
+\[
+C\dot T=G(T_H-T)+G_\ell(T_C-T)\quad\hbox{on the hot contact},
+\]
+\[
+C\dot T=G(T_C-T)+G_\ell(T_H-T)\quad\hbox{on the cold contact}.
+\]
+
+Writing (T_H^*=(GT_H+G_\ell T_C)/(G+G_\ell)) and (T_C^*=(GT_C+G_\ell T_H)/(G+G_\ell)), sustained switching is possible in this model **only if**
+
+\[
+T_C^*<T_\downarrow<T_\uparrow<T_H^*.
+\tag{1}
+\]
+
+This is a genuine coexistence test: a material may have a large polarization change and a relay may switch on a benchtop, yet the installed off-state thermal leak can make the two terminal temperatures unreachable. If (1) holds and switching is fast, the hot and cold dwell times are
+
+\[
+t_H={C\over G+G_\ell}\log {T_H^*-T_\downarrow\over T_H^*-T_\uparrow},\qquad
+t_C={C\over G+G_\ell}\log {T_\uparrow-T_C^*\over T_\downarrow-T_C^*}.
+\tag{2}
+\]
+
+The actual period adds valve travel, thermal lag and any regeneration dwell. These equations follow by solving the linear heat-balance ODE; they are not a claim that real ferroelectric thermal response is single-exponential. They show why a relay that follows local temperature cannot promise 0.2 Hz without acquiring (C,G,G_\ell) and the contact delays. The explicitly hypothetical values in [calculation output](CALCULATIONS.json) give about 0.039 Hz despite 80 K reservoir span; they are a sensitivity example, not device data. Electrocaloric temperature jumps at field changes can also drive relay chatter unless the post-switch state remains inside the hysteresis band.
+
+For a measured electric-displacement loop (D(E,T)), the *signed electrical work delivered by the bank* is the cycle integral (w_e=-\oint E\,dD) per active volume, with the sign fixed by measured terminal voltage/current. In a rectangular small-signal approximation with cold-to-hot polarization decrease (\Delta P>0), high/low fields (E_H>E_L), and active volume (V_a), the available work is approximately
+
+\[
+W_{\rm loop}\simeq V_a(E_H-E_L)\Delta P,
+\tag{3}
+\]
+
+before leakage, hysteretic loss, switching, rectification and mechanical work. The exact signed loop, not an assumed favorable \(\Delta P\), must be acquired at operating frequency and temperature. Antiphase charge transfer reduces gross charging loss but does not change the cycle's heat-to-work exergy limit. For hot heat (Q_H>0), the net electrical work of a periodic device obeys (W_{\rm DC}\le Q_H(1-T_C/T_H)) for ideal fixed-temperature reservoirs; finite stream temperatures and other exergy inputs need a stream-exergy ledger. A more operational accounting is
+
+\[
+P_{\rm exported}=fW_{\rm bank,measured}-P_{\rm field\ electronics}
+-P_{\rm pump}-P_{\rm relay/valves}-P_{\rm standby}-P_{\rm conditioning},
+\tag{4}
+\]
+
+where the bank's measured signed work already includes field charge returned to storage; each term must be measured once, avoiding double counting. If the relay/valve is driven directly by thermal motion, its cost appears as reduced (Q_H)-to-electric conversion and heat rejection, not as a fictitious zero-work port.
+
+For two equal lumped banks initially at (T_H,T_C), direct passive contact transfers at most (C(T_H-T_C)/2) from the hot bank to the cold bank before they meet at the mean temperature. Thus one lumped equalization can recover at most half of the sensible heat of a full temperature swing; finite-time transfer recovers less. A staged counterflow regenerator could do better, but adds contact area, heat capacity, pressure drop and cycle time. Regeneration changes hot heat demand, not the source of electrical work.
+
+## Quantitative power coexistence screen
+
+The 2026 *Joule* primary paper reports GEN3 at **1 W electrical output**, **0.2 Hz**, 255 PST multilayer capacitors and 4.3 cm³ active material; this is **5 J per cycle at the reported electric output port**. It uses a two-fluid-loop hot/cold switching system and high voltage (350 V at GEN3). Its separate Stirling-cycle demonstrator powers communication electronics, but its published 1 W headline is not evidence that *this passive relay assembly* delivers 1 W net after fluid handling and voltage conversion. The 2022 *Nature* paper reports 54 mW for a 57 s actively pumped/valved Olsen cycle and a best reported module heat-to-electric efficiency of 1.43% at its own operating point. The 2012 bimetal/pyroelectric primary paper reports 4.4 µW at 0.19 Hz across 96 K. These are **three different devices/conditions**; combining their best numbers is invalid as a performance estimate.
+
+The potentially fatal complete-system term is fluid handling. If a water-like fluid carries hot heat (\dot Q_H=\rho c_p\dot V\Delta T_f) and a pump overcomes pressure drop (\Delta p) at efficiency (\eta_p), then
+
+\[
+{P_{\rm pump}\over\dot Q_H}={\Delta p\over \rho c_p\Delta T_f\eta_p}.
+\tag{5}
+\]
+
+For an illustrative 1.43% conversion fraction (borrowed from the **different 2022 point**), \(\rho c_p=4.2\times10^6\) J m⁻³ K⁻¹, \(\Delta T_f=10\) K and \(\eta_p=0.30\), pumping alone consumes the entire gross output if \(\Delta p\ge180\) kPa. At 100 kPa, the hypothetical 1 W gross output would need about 70 W hot heat and 0.555 W pump input, leaving 0.445 W before all other costs. At 200 kPa with a 5 K fluid temperature change, pumping would consume 2.22 W. The arithmetic is in [calculations.py](calculations.py) and [CALCULATIONS.json](CALCULATIONS.json). None of those pressure drop, efficiency, flow or heat numbers was acquired for the 2026 generator; the screen says exactly what must be met, **not** that its full system fails.
+
+One redesign is a gravity/thermosiphon loop plus a small thermally switched valve, avoiding powered pumping. It still requires two complete heat-exchanger loops, a finite buoyancy head, check-valve losses, and reliable alternation; a passive heat pipe's continuous hot-to-cold transport is not automatically alternating contact to the ferroelectric. The 2012 bimetal experiment proves only µW output from a directly moved small element. The 2026 thermomagnetic self-oscillator gives a useful independent warning: it reports 0.8 µW peak AC and 1.25 µW cm⁻² DC after rectification, with simulated heat intake 180–800 mW across its geometries and dominant mechanical/impact damping. Its self-tuning temperature window is real, yet sensorless oscillation alone did not create high conversion power. A heat-driven relay must therefore be measured with the high-throughput bank and fluid path; low-power self-oscillation and high-power loop output cannot be spliced into a successful device.
+
+## Strongest equally informed competitors and substantive fallback
+
+**Closest incumbent:** The active fluid-cycled PST Olsen generator of Song et al. (2026), with the *same* characterized capacitors, reservoirs, flow path, electrical recovery, and field limits. Give its controller access to the same local temperatures and terminal power. It can use thermocouples or terminal-based extremum seeking to adjust phase and field, including thermal drift. The proposed relay wins only if it exports more net DC, or the same service at lower total lifetime cost/failure rate, after its extra relay and losses are charged. Standard inductor charge transfer between antiphase ferroelectric capacitors was demonstrated in 2018; it is not an invention credit here. A same-footprint thermoelectric generator (TEG), with its own optimized heat exchangers and converter, is the alternative service competitor.
+
+The failure mode prompted a substantive simpler fallback: **direct TEG with a fixed, uncertainty-robust electrical load**. If its acquired terminal characteristic over the *actual thermal boundary* is Thevenin (V=E-rI), (E>0), (r\in[r_-,r_+]), choose a passive load (R=\sqrt{r_-r_+}). Then (P=E^2R/(r+R)^2), while the instantaneous ideal matched power is (E^2/(4r)), so
+
+\[
+{P\over P_{\max}}={4rR\over(r+R)^2}
+\ge {4\sqrt\kappa\over(1+\sqrt\kappa)^2},\qquad
+\kappa=r_+/r_-.
+\tag{6}
+\]
+
+For a fourfold acquired resistance range the guaranteed fraction is 8/9; for sixteenfold it is 0.64. This is a complete elementary circuit derivation under its stated port model, not a discovery or a guarantee that unknown thermal contacts leave a linear Thevenin source. It shows that hiding microscopic pathways need not prevent positive power if the *port response* is acquired. It also removes the relay, thermal cycling, high-voltage bias, and active timing. A 2015 primary TEG MPPT study already reports 1.87% average deviation from maximum-power output, so the fixed-load theorem gives no evident matched advantage. The TEG's low-grade efficiency and heat-exchanger burden must still be measured at the service terminals.
+
+## Fatal experiment and acquisition ledger
+
+Build the candidate and the active PST incumbent with identical banks, heat exchangers, inlet streams, coolant pressure budget, power electronics and storage. Randomize time blocks across control modes: (i) thermal relay, (ii) active controller with the **same** local temperature/terminal information, and (iii) a fixed schedule. Include a commercial/optimized TEG assembly at matched footprint, streams and sink as the service comparator. Meter simultaneous (Q_H,Q_C), bank (V,I), storage (V,I), pump/valve/controller power, pressure and flow, relay position/temperature, and failure/downtime. Run long enough to separate startup charge depletion and fatigue from sustained output. The decisive pass condition is positive storage-bus energy growth under load over many steady cycles, no external unmetered clock/field/pump supply, and a statistically resolved net/lifetime advantage at the same service. An equally informed active controller reaching the same or higher net output at comparable cost kills the claimed control advantage even if the passive cycle works. If (1) fails in operation, if the relay phase differs from the terminal optimum, or if (4) is nonpositive, the operation fails its own physical gate.
+
+Acquisition and cost items that must remain explicit: ferroelectric batch yield and frequency-dependent full (D(E,T)) loops; latent/sensible heat and hysteresis; (C,G,G_\ell) including contacts and valves; local temperature relay lag and electrocaloric jumps; field supply and dielectric breakdown; electrical charge-transfer loss; hot/cold stream enthalpy and exergy; pump/thermosiphon hydraulic loss; cold-side heat rejection; insulation, leakage, pressure sealing and fouling; startup inventory; sensor/meter calibration used to *certify* output; footprint and active-material manufacture; and cyclic fatigue of both relay and capacitors. The controller may use fewer electronic sensors, but the bench must still instrument all energy ports to verify the claim.
+

+"""Arithmetic screens for the energy/control report.
+
+These are conditional engineering examples, not predictions of an integrated
+device. The 1 W, 0.2 Hz and 1.43% numbers came from different published
+operating points and are deliberately kept as separate labels in the output.
+"""
+
+import json
+import math
+from pathlib import Path
+
+
+def pump_fraction(delta_p_pa, rho_cp_j_m3_k, fluid_delta_t_k, pump_efficiency):
+    return delta_p_pa / (rho_cp_j_m3_k * fluid_delta_t_k * pump_efficiency)
+
+
+def robust_fraction(resistance_ratio):
+    root = math.sqrt(resistance_ratio)
+    return 4 * root / (1 + root) ** 2
+
+
+def thermal_clock(th, tc, t_up, t_down, c, g_on, g_leak):
+    g_total = g_on + g_leak
+    hot_limit = (g_on * th + g_leak * tc) / g_total
+    cold_limit = (g_on * tc + g_leak * th) / g_total
+    if not (cold_limit < t_down < t_up < hot_limit):
+        return {"oscillates": False, "hot_limit_K": hot_limit, "cold_limit_K": cold_limit}
+    hot_time = c / g_total * math.log((hot_limit - t_down) / (hot_limit - t_up))
+    cold_time = c / g_total * math.log((t_up - cold_limit) / (t_down - cold_limit))
+    return {
+        "oscillates": True,
+        "hot_limit_K": hot_limit,
+        "cold_limit_K": cold_limit,
+        "hot_time_s": hot_time,
+        "cold_time_s": cold_time,
+        "frequency_Hz_before_switching_delay": 1 / (hot_time + cold_time),
+    }
+
+
+def main():
+    # 2022 Nature reports up to 1.43% module-level heat-to-electric efficiency.
+    # Treating it as if a separate 1 W generator attained that same point is
+    # explicitly a counterfactual sensitivity exercise.
+    illustrative_conversion_efficiency = 0.0143
+    reported_output_w = 1.0
+    reported_frequency_hz = 0.2
+    rho_cp = 4.2e6  # water, illustrative volumetric heat capacity J/m3/K
+    pump_eff = 0.30  # illustrative shaft-to-fluid efficiency
+    pump_cases = []
+    for dp, dt in [(100_000, 10), (200_000, 5)]:
+        f = pump_fraction(dp, rho_cp, dt, pump_eff)
+        pump_cases.append(
+            {
+                "pressure_drop_Pa": dp,
+                "fluid_delta_T_K": dt,
+                "pump_fraction_of_hot_heat": f,
+                "illustrative_hot_heat_for_1_W_W": reported_output_w / illustrative_conversion_efficiency,
+                "illustrative_pump_W": f * reported_output_w / illustrative_conversion_efficiency,
+                "illustrative_net_before_other_losses_W": reported_output_w
+                - f * reported_output_w / illustrative_conversion_efficiency,
+            }
+        )
+    output = {
+        "provenance_note": "Conditional arithmetic only; 1 W at 0.2 Hz is the 2026 Joule report, whereas 1.43% is a 2022 Nature best efficiency at a different operating point. Neither paper measured the hybrid device.",
+        "source_reported_1W_at_0p2Hz_implies_J_per_cycle": reported_output_w / reported_frequency_hz,
+        "pump_break_even_pressure_Pa_at_10K": illustrative_conversion_efficiency * rho_cp * 10 * pump_eff,
+        "pump_break_even_pressure_Pa_at_5K": illustrative_conversion_efficiency * rho_cp * 5 * pump_eff,
+        "pump_cases": pump_cases,
+        "thermal_clock_illustration_not_device_data": thermal_clock(
+            th=373.15,
+            tc=293.15,
+            t_up=353.15,
+            t_down=313.15,
+            c=10.0,
+            g_on=1.0,
+            g_leak=0.1,
+        ),
+        "fixed_load_min_fraction_at_Rs_ratio_4": robust_fraction(4),
+        "fixed_load_min_fraction_at_Rs_ratio_16": robust_fraction(16),
+    }
+    out_path = Path(__file__).with_name("CALCULATIONS.json")
+    out_path.write_text(json.dumps(output, indent=2, sort_keys=True) + "\n")
+    print(out_path)
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    main()

+# S07 — physically enrich a rare catalytic state, then infer its native flux
+
+15 October 2026, Australia/Brisbane. **Status: conditional construction; no demonstrated new capability, full-cost advantage, or novelty.** The earlier hidden-terminal-row search bound concerns a local-row oracle. It does not apply when a real catalyst offers a reversible field or ligand control that changes the population of a chemically identified intermediate, plus independent product and spectroscopic readouts. I investigated that richer interface for a molecular CO₂-to-formate catalyst. The proposed output is the *native*, per-active-site formate initiation rate and the hydride-state contribution at a specified potential, proton activity, CO₂ activity, temperature and electrode geometry. It is not a measured rate in this report.
+
+## Operation and the access it uses
+
+Take a catalyst whose resting state `A` interconverts with a metal-hydride state `I`; `I` can return to `A`, make formate, or make H₂. At a low operating potential, `I` may be too sparsely populated to characterize directly even though its chemical identity controls selectivity. The concrete intervention is a **paired potential-gate and release assay**:
+
+1. Under conditions that suppress **both** formate and H₂ exits without changing the bare `A↔I` chemistry, titrate potential through overlapping windows until the `A:I` ratio is measurable by a calibrated state-resolved spectrum or electrochemical signal. Recover the rare ratio at the operating potential from the measured electrochemical free-energy difference. This physically prepares an enriched `I` ensemble; it assumes no ability to set an arbitrary microscopic state. Simultaneously suppressing both exits is itself an unverified chemical feasibility gate.
+2. On matched catalyst aliquots under native CO₂/proton/electrolyte conditions, apply a brief enrichment pulse to one and a sham pulse to the other. Return both to the *same controlled operating potential*, not open circuit. Record the difference in the hydride signal and time-resolved formate and H₂ flux. The formate signal can be isotope-resolved if source attribution is needed, with the isotope effect calibrated separately.
+3. Infer the native state-entry rate and formate flux from the reaction-off equilibrium odds and the native differential decay. This uses the physical ability to accumulate and read out many `I` states simultaneously. It requires state identity, electrical control, and a closed kinetic model; it does not infer the rate from a pulse burst alone.
+
+Metal-hydride pre-equilibrium and its control of formate formation are physically motivated by Pattanayak and Berben's [primary CO₂-reduction study](https://doi.org/10.1021/jacs.2c10942): the accessible article text describes a metal carbonyl cluster, fast hydride formation, competing H₂ formation and a formate-rate law involving a hydride-formation equilibrium. It reports up to 296 s⁻¹ formate production in its conditions. **That paper does not establish that its hydride is rare at my proposed operating point, nor that the pulse protocol below works on that complex.** It also makes the central pre-equilibrium idea and much of the chemistry clear prior art. The [2018 stopped-flow metal-hydride study](https://doi.org/10.1039/C8SC02535E) reports experimental CO₂-insertion kinetics and ligand/solvent effects, supporting a possible fast continuation readout but warning that its rate depends on chemistry. A recent [IrOₓ operando study](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41563-026-02514-9) actually combines potential steps, time-resolved optical and X-ray spectroscopy, charge accounting and EC-MS oxygen measurement. Its pulse readout is an unusually strong empirical comparator; it also reports a nonlinear rate versus accumulated O⁻ coverage, so the two-state formula below must **not** simply be applied to IrOₓ.
+
+## Exact rate identity in the smallest closed model
+
+This is an original derivation for the stated idealized continuous-time model, not a claim that any real catalyst obeys it. Each active site is in `A` or `I`. At native conditions, `A→I` has hazard `α`, and `I→A` has reversible hazard `β`. From `I`, formate initiation has hazard `γ` and H₂ initiation hazard `δ`; each product event resets the site immediately to `A`. Rates are constant over the assay; sites do not interact; transport and site loss are absent. The product-free reversible pair has odds
+
+\[
+K_0 = {\alpha\over\beta} = {P_{\rm off}(I)\over P_{\rm off}(A)}. \tag{1}
+\]
+
+The nontrivial transport premise is that adding CO₂ and running the native reaction leaves the *bare* `A↔I` hazards `α,β` unchanged. H₂ is included explicitly because it competes with formate in a metal-hydride catalyst; any additional exit needs its own measured hazard. Under native conditions, if `m(t)=P(I,t)`,
+
+\[
+\dot m=\alpha(1-m)-(\beta+\gamma+\delta)m
+       =\alpha-Rm,\qquad R=\alpha+\beta+\gamma+\delta. \tag{2}
+\]
+
+For a pulse and sham sample that differ only in initial `I` fraction, `Δm(t)=Δm(0)e^{-Rt}`. The excess product initiation rates are `Δj_F(t)=γ Δm(t)` and `Δj_H(t)=δ Δm(t)`. Thus `R` comes from the common exponential, while `γ=Δj_F/Δm` and `δ=Δj_H/Δm` come from calibrated differential products; these ratios can use an integrated burst if detector impulse responses are deconvolved. Solving (1)–(2),
+
+\[
+\beta={R-\gamma-\delta\over 1+K_0},\qquad
+\alpha={K_0(R-\gamma-\delta)\over1+K_0},\qquad
+\boxed{j_F^{(0)}={\gamma K_0(R-\gamma-\delta)\over(1+K_0)R}}. \tag{3}
+\]
+
+Here `j_F^(0)` is the *unperturbed/native* steady formate initiation rate per available site. Equation (3) does not use a pre-equilibrium approximation such as `γ≪β`; it explicitly accounts for product removal of `I`. A negative reconstructed `β` or a non-single-exponential difference is an immediate model-failure diagnostic. If product release or catalyst recovery consumes appreciable time, a third state is required and (3) is not the turnover frequency.
+If a parallel formate route leaves directly from `A`, (3) estimates only the hydride-mediated component; total formate flux needs that route's separate rate. This distinction makes pathway attribution the scientifically useful output when direct bulk formate is already countable.
+
+At potentials `E₁` where the reaction-off odds are measurable, thermodynamic transport to `E₀` uses the acquired conjugate charge, activities and temperature:
+
+\[
+\log K_0=\log K(E_1)-{1\over k_{\rm B}T}
+                 \int_{E_0}^{E_1}\Delta Q(E)\,dE. \tag{4}
+\]
+
+`ΔQ(E)` is the equilibrium charge difference of the identified `I` and `A` states, including proton/electrolyte linkage if these change. The common Nernst simplification `ΔQ=e` is valid only for a single fixed one-electron transition at fixed relevant activities. A field-created hydride with a changed ligand, oxidation state, solvation shell or site distribution is not the native `I`. Equation (4) is a thermodynamic identity within the specified equilibrium family; the applicability of that family is an experimental burden. Its uncertainty is additive in `log K₀` and becomes multiplicative in the rare rate.
+
+This separates two physical ways to gain access: potential control increases `I` population during measurement, and parallel catalyst sites make the product burst measurable in a short window. Neither is free. If `K₀≪1` and `γ/(β+γ+δ)` is order one, an ideal native product counter needs exposure of order `1/[M j_F^(0) ε²]` for relative error `ε` on `M` independent sites. The pulse can yield order `M Δm(0)γ/R` extra product molecules in one relaxation, while equilibrium titration obtains a tiny `K₀` through intermediate-occupancy windows. This comparison is only an information-scale illustration. It excludes chemical drift, correlated sites, detector background and the full apparatus costs below; it does not prove a practical speedup. If `γ/R` is also tiny, product-burst counting still needs order `1/(γ/R)` enriched site-continuations per observed product.
+
+## What an easier trap would and would not identify
+
+I first examined adding a state-specific stable chemical trap at pseudo-first-order hazard `cκ`. In the same two-state cycle it produces
+
+\[
+j_T(c)={\alpha c\kappa\over\alpha+\beta+\gamma+\delta+c\kappa}.
+\]
+
+This is useful: stable adducts can integrate a fleeting-state signal, and a dose series can infer `α` and `α+β+γ+δ` if `κ`, trap specificity and response are independently calibrated. It cannot split `β`, `γ` and `δ`, so trap signal alone cannot determine unperturbed formate flux. High-dose trapping also changes occupancy and diverts product. At low dose the mark rate vanishes with `c`, so an apparent sensitivity gain must pay in site-time. Spin-trap research supplies a real warning: [an isotope-order artifact experiment](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3859841/) found false signals arising from non-radical addition followed by oxidation under some conditions. The trap is therefore a discovery/identity control, not a sufficient kinetic estimator. The gated equilibrium plus native release is the substantive redesign after this identification failure.
+
+## Exact counterexample to an unjustified transport
+

+"""Exact toy algebra for the proposed catalyst pulse/thermodynamic relay.
+
+No experimental observations are represented here.  Run with Python 3's
+standard library: python3 exact_fixture.py
+"""
+
+from fractions import Fraction as F
+from json import dumps
+
+
+def native(alpha, beta, gamma, delta=F(0)):
+    total = alpha + beta + gamma + delta
+    return {
+        "R": total,
+        "steady_I": alpha / total,
+        "formate_flux": alpha * gamma / total,
+        "hydrogen_flux": alpha * delta / total,
+    }
+
+
+def reconstructed(K, R, gamma, delta=F(0)):
+    beta = (R - gamma - delta) / (1 + K)
+    alpha = K * beta
+    return native(alpha, beta, gamma, delta)
+
+
+def out(d):
+    return {k: {"exact": str(v), "decimal": float(v)} for k, v in d.items()}
+
+
+K_off = F(1, 1_000_000)
+alpha_off = F(1, 100_000)
+beta_off = F(10)
+gamma = F(1)
+
+# Transport-valid world: native formation/reversal equal the product-free pair.
+world_0 = native(alpha_off, beta_off, gamma)
+recovered_0 = reconstructed(K_off, world_0["R"], gamma)
+assert world_0 == recovered_0
+
+# An unobserved substrate effect doubles native formation and compensates in
+# native reversal, so the pulse relaxation R and product slope gamma are the
+# same.  The product-free titration remains unchanged.
+alpha_1 = F(2, 100_000)
+beta_1 = world_0["R"] - gamma - alpha_1
+world_1 = native(alpha_1, beta_1, gamma)
+assert world_1["R"] == world_0["R"]
+assert world_1["formate_flux"] == 2 * world_0["formate_flux"]
+
+print(dumps({
+    "status": "exact toy algebra only; no physical data",
+    "product_free_K": str(K_off),
+    "pulse_observables_common_to_both_worlds": {
+        "R": str(world_0["R"]), "gamma": str(gamma)
+    },
+    "transport_valid_world": out(world_0),
+    "transport_failed_world": out(world_1),
+    "formula_infers_world_0_from_common_observables": out(recovered_0),
+}, indent=2))

This is a lower bound, not the optimum or a proof of finite-dimensional attainment. Let $P$ and $P^*$ be the stationary microscopic path laws of $Q$ and $Q^*$ on $[-t,t]$. Their arithmetic and geometric path measures are
+$$
+\mu=(P+P^*)/2,\qquad d\nu=\sqrt{dP\,dP^*},\qquad A=\nu(\Omega)\le1.
+$$
+Taking a common dominating measure gives $d(\mu-\nu)=\tfrac12(\sqrt{dP}-\sqrt{dP^*})^2\ge0$, of total mass $1-A$. Thus the signed subtraction used by the certificate is actually a **positive measure**.
+
+For a CTMC trajectory, its initial-state factor is $\pi_i$ under both laws, each holding-time factor is $e^{Q_{ii}\tau}$ under both, and a jump $i\to j$ contributes $\sqrt{Q_{ij}Q^*_{ij}}$ to $\nu$. Consequently $\nu$ is represented by the sub-Markov generator
+$$
+G_{ii}=Q_{ii},\qquad G_{ij}=\sqrt{Q_{ij}Q^*_{ij}}\quad(i\ne j).
+$$
+It is genuinely sub-Markov: $\sum_jG_{ij}\le Q_{ii}+\tfrac12\sum_{j\ne i}(Q_{ij}+Q^*_{ij})=0$. Further,
+$$
+\pi_iG_{ij}=\sqrt{\pi_iQ_{ij}\,\pi_jQ_{ji}}=\pi_jG_{ji},
+$$
+so $G$ and $e^{tG}$ are self-adjoint in $L^2(\pi)$. No normalization of $\nu$ is inserted; doing so would lose the killing mass $1-A$ and spoil the argument.
+
+Fix a visible block $B$, any $a\in(0,1)$, $f=\mathbf1_B-a\mathbf1$, and the three-time witness
+$$
+W=\mathbf1_B(X_0)f(X_{-t})f(X_t).
+$$
+Time reflection swaps the two endpoint factors and leaves $W$ unchanged. Because $P^*$ is the reflected law of stationary $P$, $\mathbb E_\mu W=\mathbb E_PW$. The geometric measure gives a nonnegative square:
+$$
+\mathbb E_\nu W=\langle f,e^{tG}\operatorname{diag}(\mathbf1_B)e^{tG}f\rangle_\pi
+=\sum_{i\in B}\pi_i[(e^{tG}f)_i]^2\ge0.

+Here the central-state factorization is legitimate for the killed semigroup; it does not assert conditional independence after normalizing $\nu$. Since $W\ge-a(1-a)$, if the observed law fixes $\mathbb E_PW=-D<0$, then
+$$
+-D=\mathbb E_\nu W+\mathbb E_{\mu-\nu}W
+\ge-a(1-a)(1-A),\qquad D\le a(1-a)(1-A). \tag{1}
+$$

+$$
+\boxed{\displaystyle \sigma(Q)\ge-\frac1t\log\left(1-\frac{D}{a(1-a)}\right).} \tag{2}

Cloning or weighted-ensemble resampling of *native* trajectories can instead retain native path statistics when correctly weighted; [Zhang, Jasnow and Zuckerman, 2010](https://doi.org/10.1063/1.3306345) establish a broad path-sampling exactness result. Neither procedure generates information about $H_0$ versus $H_1$ from the identical $Q$ transcript. If native trajectories are available, the single-step fixture provides no intermediate interface to exploit; its rare-channel exposure cost remains explicit. For systems with informative interfaces, [forward-flux sampling](https://arxiv.org/abs/cond-mat/0602269) and weighted ensembles are serious matched comparators, not ruled out by this toy.
+
+## Substantive repair: complementary probes with a rank and coverage certificate
+
+The obstruction is a missing identifiable contrast. Here is a *conditional* redesign that supplies one. Suppose there are finitely many candidate native channel rates λ and controlled nuisance creation rates $c$, and each control (a) has a *calibrated* linear intensity response $r_a=M_a\theta$, where θ stacks those unknown rates. Unmarked event counts suffice. For target native total $R=t^\top\theta$, an unlimited-precision collection of controlled rate measurements identifies $R$ for all interior admissible θ **if and only if** $t$ lies in the row space of the combined response matrix $M$. Sufficiency follows from $t=w^\top M$, giving $R=w^\top r$. Conversely, if $t\notin\operatorname{row}(M)$, some $v\in\ker M$ has $t^\top v\ne0$; two nearby nonnegative parameter vectors θ and θ+δv have identical controlled data but different native totals. This is exact linear algebra, with no asymptotic sampling claim beyond intensity identification.
+
+A concrete three-probe repair of the fixture has unknown $\theta=(\lambda_x,\lambda_y,\gamma)$ and measured *unmarked* total intensities
+
+\[
+r_1=b\lambda_x+\gamma,\qquad
+r_2=b\lambda_y+\gamma,\qquad
+r_3=\gamma,\qquad
+R=\lambda_x+\lambda_y=\frac{r_1+r_2-2r_3}{b}.
+\]
+
+Probe 2 exposes the formerly suppressed native $y$ channel; probe 3 calibrates the control-created background. With only probes 1 and 2, the direction $(-1/b,-1/b,1)$ leaves both measured rates fixed while changing $R$ by $-2/b$. Thus even a complementary native-channel probe is insufficient if the synthetic route is unmeasured. Alternatively, reliable channel labeling and a control-created-route classification could remove the nuisance without probe 3, but those are acquired observations and classifications.
+
+For independent Poisson event counts $N_i$ over controlled exposures $T_i$, $\widehat R=(N_1/T_1+N_2/T_2-2N_3/T_3)/b$ is unbiased under this model and has exact variance
+
+\[
+\operatorname{Var}(\widehat R)=\frac{r_1/T_1+r_2/T_2+4r_3/T_3}{b^2}.
+\]
+
+This can beat native waiting for *statistical* precision if the boost is large and the nuisance small, but it is not free. In the rational fixture λ_x=λ_y=1/1024, $b=64,γ=1/64$, each probe has $T_i=16384$. The exact totals are $(5/64,5/64,1/64)$, $R=1/512$, and relative variance $7/8192\approx0.00085449$. A native Poisson count over the **same aggregate exposure** $3T_i=49152$ has relative variance $1/96\approx0.0104167$. The controlled ratio is $21/256\approx0.0820$. Yet those controlled runs cause 2816 expected events versus 96 native events: reset, sensing and reaction-energy costs may reverse the apparent gain. A stronger native simulator with exact generator rows computes $R$ without sampling in this fixture.
+
+The repair also needs a **support ledger**. If an unmodeled native channel carries unknown total hazard Δ, the reconstruction covers only $R_\mathrm{known}$ and the actual total is $R_\mathrm{known}+Δ$. A separately validated upper bound $0\leqΔ\leq U$ yields an honest interval $[R_\mathrm{known},R_\mathrm{known}+U]$. If $U$ is comparable to $R_\mathrm{known}$, it cannot rule out the factor-two counterexample. Acquiring a strong $U$, validating the response matrix across all relevant pathways, and detecting control-created chemistry are the substantive unsolved parts. The three-probe algebra by itself does not do them.
+

It can prepend the same three-probe linear reconstruction. No new algorithmic or physical advantage over that comparator is established. +#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Exact rational interval certificate for q=1/20 at h=1/5.
+
+No floating-point arithmetic is used in any assertion.  Decimal printing at
+the end is display only.  The exponential interval uses the alternating
+Taylor series for exp(-x), valid here because 0 <= x < 1.
+"""
+
+from dataclasses import dataclass
+from decimal import Decimal, getcontext
+from fractions import Fraction as F
+from math import factorial
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class I:
+    lo: F
+    hi: F
+
+    def __post_init__(self):
+        assert self.lo <= self.hi
+
+    @staticmethod
+    def of(x):
+        return x if isinstance(x, I) else I(F(x), F(x))
+
+    def __add__(self, other):
+        other = I.of(other)
+        return I(self.lo + other.lo, self.hi + other.hi)
+
+    __radd__ = __add__
+
+    def __neg__(self):
+        return I(-self.hi, -self.lo)
+
+    def __sub__(self, other):
+        return self + (-I.of(other))
+
+    def __rsub__(self, other):
+        return I.of(other) - self
+
+    def __mul__(self, other):
+        other = I.of(other)
+        products = [a * b for a in (self.lo, self.hi) for b in (other.lo, other.hi)]
+        return I(min(products), max(products))
+
+    __rmul__ = __mul__
+
+    def __truediv__(self, other):
+        other = I.of(other)
+        assert 0 < other.lo
+        return self * I(F(1) / other.hi, F(1) / other.lo)
+
+    def __pow__(self, power):
+        assert isinstance(power, int) and power >= 0
+        result = I.of(1)
+        for _ in range(power):
+            result *= self
+        return result
+
+
+def alternating_sum(x: F, order: int) -> F:
+    return sum(((-x) ** k / factorial(k) for k in range(order + 1)), F(0))
+
+
+def exp_minus(x: I) -> I:
+    assert 0 <= x.lo <= x.hi < 1
+    # Odd truncation is below exp(-x), even truncation above it.
+    return I(alternating_sum(x.hi, 19), alternating_sum(x.lo, 18))
+
+
+q = F(1, 20)
+sqrt_q_lo = F(22360679774997896964, 10**20)
+sqrt_q_hi = F(22360679774997896965, 10**20)
+assert sqrt_q_lo**2 < q < sqrt_q_hi**2
+sqrt_q = I(sqrt_q_lo, sqrt_q_hi)
+
+s = F(1) + q
+b = 2 * q / s
+c = F(1) + q + q**2
+mean_b = (2 * s - b) / c  # minus derivative at zero of the Laplace transform
+assert mean_b == 2 / s
+ell = s - sqrt_q
+high = s + sqrt_q
+denom = high - ell
+a_pos = (c - b * ell) / denom
+a_neg = (b * high - c) / denom
+assert a_pos.lo > 0 and a_neg.hi < 0
+assert a_pos.lo + a_neg.lo <= b <= a_pos.hi + a_neg.hi
+
+entry_rate = s / 3
+f_prime_zero = c - b * 2 * s
+assert f_prime_zero == F(341, 400)
+stationary_third_derivative = entry_rate * f_prime_zero
+assert entry_rate == F(7, 20)
+assert stationary_third_derivative == F(2387, 8000)
+stationary_b_mass = entry_rate * mean_b
+assert stationary_b_mass == F(2, 3)
+stationary_no_exit_at_zero = entry_rate * (
+    a_pos / (ell**2) + a_neg / (high**2)
+)
+assert stationary_no_exit_at_zero.lo < stationary_b_mass < stationary_no_exit_at_zero.hi
+
+h = F(1, 5)
+e_ell = exp_minus(ell * h)
+e_high = exp_minus(high * h)
+delta_three = entry_rate * (
+    (a_pos / (ell**2)) * ((e_ell - 1) ** 3)
+    + (a_neg / (high**2)) * ((e_high - 1) ** 3)
+)
+assert delta_three.lo > F(1, 1000)
+assert delta_three.hi < F(12, 10000)
+
+# For a width-three witness on [0,3h], Pinsker and the KL/EP comparison
+# give sigma >= 8*d^2/(27*h).  The strict d lower bound gives:
+sigma_lower = 8 * F(1, 1000) ** 2 / (27 * h)
+assert sigma_lower == F(1, 675000)
+
+getcontext().prec = 30
+as_decimal = lambda x: Decimal(x.numerator) / Decimal(x.denominator)
+print("sqrt(q) interval:", as_decimal(sqrt_q.lo), as_decimal(sqrt_q.hi))
+print("f_B'(0):", f_prime_zero)
+print("A_B'''(0):", stationary_third_derivative)
+print("stationary B mass:", stationary_b_mass)
+print("Delta^3 A_B(0), h=1/5 interval:", as_decimal(delta_three.lo), as_decimal(delta_three.hi))
+print("rigorous all-dimension EP lower bound: sigma > 1/675000")

+"""Exact rational checks for the intervention/native-rate counterexample.
+
+No stochastic sample or physical experiment is simulated.  The Poisson variance
+calculation assumes independent, instantly resettable controlled preparations.
+"""
+
+from fractions import Fraction as F
+
+
+def dot(row, vector):
+    return sum((a * b for a, b in zip(row, vector)), F(0))
+
+
+epsilon = F(1, 1024)
+boost = F(64)
+gamma = F(1, 64)
+native_0 = (epsilon, F(0), F(0))  # x, y, z
+native_1 = (epsilon, epsilon, F(0))
+controlled_0 = (boost * epsilon, F(0), gamma)
+controlled_1 = (boost * epsilon, F(0), gamma)
+assert controlled_0 == controlled_1
+assert sum(native_1) == 2 * sum(native_0)
+
+# Unknown parameter vector theta=(native x, native y, synthetic control z).
+# Only unmarked total event counts are used in the witness-control assay.
+probe_rows = (
+    (boost, F(0), F(1)),  # x exposed, y suppressed
+    (F(0), boost, F(1)),  # y exposed, x suppressed
+    (F(0), F(0), F(1)),  # synthetic-route calibration
+)
+target = (F(1), F(1), F(0))
+combination = (F(1) / boost, F(1) / boost, -F(2) / boost)
+assert tuple(sum((combination[i] * probe_rows[i][j] for i in range(3)), F(0)) for j in range(3)) == target
+
+# Without the third probe, this direction changes the native rate but leaves
+# both controlled total rates invariant: acquisition of the nuisance is essential.
+unidentified_direction = (-F(1) / boost, -F(1) / boost, F(1))
+assert all(dot(row, unidentified_direction) == 0 for row in probe_rows[:2])
+assert dot(target, unidentified_direction) == -F(2) / boost
+
+theta = (epsilon, epsilon, gamma)
+q = [dot(row, theta) for row in probe_rows]
+assert q == [F(5, 64), F(5, 64), F(1, 64)]
+reconstructed_rate = sum((combination[i] * q[i] for i in range(3)), F(0))
+assert reconstructed_rate == 2 * epsilon == F(1, 512)
+
+# Equal exposure in each controlled probe.  This is statistical variance only;
+# it omits setup, calibration, resetting, actuation and energy costs.
+exposure_each = F(16384)
+controlled_variance = sum((combination[i] ** 2 * q[i] / exposure_each for i in range(3)), F(0))
+controlled_relative_variance = controlled_variance / reconstructed_rate**2
+native_exposure = 3 * exposure_each
+native_relative_variance = F(1) / (reconstructed_rate * native_exposure)
+assert controlled_relative_variance == F(7, 8192)
+assert native_relative_variance == F(1, 96)
+
+print(f"native rates: H0={sum(native_0)}, H1={sum(native_1)}")
+print(f"identical intervention intensities: {controlled_0}")
+print(f"probe totals: {', '.join(map(str, q))}")
+print(f"reconstructed H1 native rate: {reconstructed_rate}")
+print(f"controlled relative variance at 3 x {exposure_each} exposure: {controlled_relative_variance}")
+print(f"native relative variance at {native_exposure} exposure: {native_relative_variance}")
+print(f"controlled/native relative-variance ratio: {controlled_relative_variance / native_relative_variance}")

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Exact rational intervals for the geometric-affinity ring witness.
+
+The three-state ring has clockwise rate 1, counterclockwise rate q=1/20,
+uniform stationary distribution, and visible set B={1,2}.  At t=3/10,
+the formulas for a and D below follow from diagonalizing the circulant
+generator.  All asserted bounds use Fraction; Decimal is display only.
+"""
+
+from dataclasses import dataclass
+from decimal import Decimal, getcontext
+from fractions import Fraction as F
+from math import factorial, isqrt
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class Interval:
+    lo: F
+    hi: F
+
+    def __post_init__(self):
+        assert self.lo <= self.hi
+
+    @staticmethod
+    def of(x):
+        return x if isinstance(x, Interval) else Interval(F(x), F(x))
+
+    def __add__(self, other):
+        other = Interval.of(other)
+        return Interval(self.lo + other.lo, self.hi + other.hi)
+
+    __radd__ = __add__
+
+    def __neg__(self):
+        return Interval(-self.hi, -self.lo)
+
+    def __sub__(self, other):
+        return self + (-Interval.of(other))
+
+    def __rsub__(self, other):
+        return Interval.of(other) - self
+
+    def __mul__(self, other):
+        other = Interval.of(other)
+        p = [a * b for a in (self.lo, self.hi) for b in (other.lo, other.hi)]
+        return Interval(min(p), max(p))
+
+    __rmul__ = __mul__
+
+    def __truediv__(self, other):
+        other = Interval.of(other)
+        assert other.lo > 0
+        return self * Interval(1 / other.hi, 1 / other.lo)
+
+
+def alt_series(x, coefficient, odd_terms=19, even_terms=20):
+    """Bounds from successive alternating partial sums for x in [0,1)."""
+    assert 0 <= x.lo <= x.hi < 1
+
+    def partial(z, last):
+        return sum((F((-1) ** k) * coefficient(z, k)
+                    for k in range(last + 1)), F(0))
+
+    # For exp(-x) and cos(x), the function decreases on this interval.
+    # For sin(x), it increases.  The caller selects endpoints below.
+    return partial, odd_terms, even_terms
+
+
+def exp_minus(x):
+    x = Interval.of(x)
+    partial, odd, even = alt_series(x, lambda z, k: z ** k / factorial(k))
+    return Interval(partial(x.hi, odd), partial(x.lo, even))
+
+
+def sin_pos(x):
+    x = Interval.of(x)
+    partial, odd, even = alt_series(
+        x, lambda z, k: z ** (2 * k + 1) / factorial(2 * k + 1)
+    )
+    return Interval(partial(x.lo, odd), partial(x.hi, even))
+
+
+def cos_pos(x):
+    x = Interval.of(x)
+    partial, odd, even = alt_series(
+        x, lambda z, k: z ** (2 * k) / factorial(2 * k)
+    )
+    return Interval(partial(x.hi, odd), partial(x.lo, even))
+
+
+def rational_sqrt_interval(n, digits=35):
+    base = 10 ** digits
+    low_int = isqrt(n * base * base)
+    out = Interval(F(low_int, base), F(low_int + 1, base))
+    assert out.lo ** 2 < n < out.hi ** 2
+    return out
+
+
+def as_decimal(x):
+    return Decimal(x.numerator) / Decimal(x.denominator)
+
+
+q = F(1, 20)
+t = F(3, 10)
+s = 1 + q
+theta = F(57, 400) * rational_sqrt_interval(3)
+assert theta.hi < F(1, 4)
+e_half = exp_minus(3 * s * t / 2)
+e_full = exp_minus(3 * s * t)
+
+# Circulant ring propagator: P_{AA}(t) = (1+2e_half*cos(theta))/3.
+# Given X_0 in B uniformly, a=P(X_t in B | X_0 in B).
+a = F(2, 3) + e_half * cos_pos(theta) / 3
+
+# The past and future B probabilities are swapped across the two B states.
+# Their conditional deviations from a are opposite; hence
+# E[1_B(X_0)(1_B(X_-t)-a)(1_B(X_t)-a)] = -D.
+# D=(2/9)e^{-3st}sin^2(theta), with theta=sqrt(3)(1-q)t/2.
+sin_theta = sin_pos(theta)
+D = F(2, 9) * e_full * (sin_theta * sin_theta)
+assert F(86, 100) < a.lo < a.hi < F(87, 100)
+assert D.lo > F(5155, 1_000_000)
+
+# a>1/2, so a(1-a) decreases as a rises.
+C = Interval(a.hi * (1 - a.hi), a.lo * (1 - a.lo))
+z = D / C
+assert z.hi < F(1, 10)
+
+# -log(1-z)=sum_{k>=1} z^k/k.  Positive partial sum bounds below;
+# tail <= z^(N+1)/[(N+1)(1-z)] bounds above.
+N = 15
+log_lower = sum((z.lo ** k / k for k in range(1, N + 1)), F(0))
+log_upper = (sum((z.hi ** k / k for k in range(1, N + 1)), F(0))
+             + z.hi ** (N + 1) / ((N + 1) * (1 - z.hi)))
+sigma_floor = Interval(log_lower / t, log_upper / t)
+assert sigma_floor.lo > F(1536, 10000)
+assert sigma_floor.hi < F(154, 1000)
+
+getcontext().prec = 40
+for name, value in [("a", a), ("D", D), ("z=D/[a(1-a)]", z),
+                    ("sigma floor", sigma_floor)]:
+    print(name, "in (", as_decimal(value.lo), ",", as_decimal(value.hi), ")")
+print("rigorous bound for every compatible finite stationary Q: sigma > 0.1536")

+# S09 follow-up — what the pulse-order NV contrast can and cannot close
+
+15 October 2026, Australia/Brisbane. This tightens [REPORT.md](REPORT.md). **Status: exact algebra and one symbolic countermodel check completed; no pulse/NV/chemical experiment completed.** The operational claim is conditional and narrow: an embedded NV field sensor may make a *specific nonlinear pulse-order contraction* available at a buried Fe3O4/Li interface. The contraction is not a chemical label, a damage forecast, an information advantage over its own raw traces, or a quantum speedup. Its value must be earned by same-electrode chemical validation and a resource-matched nonlinear incumbent.
+
+## Exact cancellation, with the required timing and reset
+
+Choose one galvanostatic template $p(t)=+1$ for $0\leq t<\tau$, $p(t)=-1$ for $\tau\leq t<2\tau$, and $p(t)=0$ thereafter. Its negative, $-p$, is the reversed order. All four arms start at the *same clock phase* after the same formation, target state of charge, open-circuit hold, baseline NV spectrum, and calibration; all are read at the same $T=2\tau+h$, after the same zero-current delay $h$. The acquisition windows, optical/microwave duty, bias field and active/reference sampling order are identical. The amplitudes are $a\in\{1,-1,r,-r\}$, with input **actual measured current** $u_a(t)=aU p(t)$, not merely a command sent to a current source. The $rU$ arms generally carry a greater ohmic burden, but neither dissipated nor net cell energy can be inferred from zero net charge; both are measured and charged to the protocol rather than silently matched by changing the waveform.
+
+Let $Y_T[u]$ be the *noiseless or conditional-mean* map from actual current history to the active-minus-reference, after-minus-before NV field estimate at time $T$. This includes specimen dynamics, optical spin readout, spectral fitting and reference subtraction. Individual photon and specimen-noise realizations need not cancel; their contrast has zero expectation under the hypothesis below. Suppose on the tested domain this full mean map is affine,
+
+\[
+Y_T[u]=b_T+L_Tu,
+\]
+
+where $L_T$ is **any** linear functional of the input waveform. It may represent arbitrary memory, a spatially heterogeneous linear state-space system, a time-varying instrument *with the same scheduled coefficients in all four arms*, and non-convolutional relaxation. No known response kernel, spectral gap, diagonalization, stationarity or single time constant is assumed. Arm-to-arm drift that changes $L_T$ is a violation, not a canceled nuisance. Then
+
+\[
+C(U)=Y_T[Up]-Y_T[-Up]=2U L_Tp,
+\quad
+K_r(U)=C(rU)-rC(U)=2rU L_Tp-2rU L_Tp=0.
+\]
+

+"""Symbolic checks for the S09 follow-up countermodels.
+
+These identities concern toy models only; they are not experimental validation.
+"""
+
+import sympy as s
+
+U, r, tau, t = s.symbols("U r tau t", positive=True)
+a, b, v, alpha, k = s.symbols("a b v alpha k", positive=True)
+lam, gamma, beta, Bs, d = s.symbols(
+    "lam gamma beta Bs d", positive=True
+)
+
+# An even-in-current thermal state has the same trajectory in both pulse orders.
+theta = a * U**2 / b * (1 - s.exp(-b * t))
+early = s.integrate(theta, (t, 0, tau))
+late = s.integrate(theta, (t, tau, 2 * tau))
+c_thermal = s.simplify(2 * k * v * alpha * U * (late - early))
+target_thermal = (
+    2 * k * v * alpha * a * U**3
+    * (1 - s.exp(-b * tau)) ** 2 / b**2
+)
+assert s.simplify(c_thermal - target_thermal) == 0
+assert s.simplify(
+    target_thermal.subs(U, r * U) - r * target_thermal
+    - (r**3 - r) * target_thermal
+) == 0
+
+# A purely linear polarization changes a local ohmic heating coefficient.
+q_early = U * (1 - s.exp(-lam * t)) / lam
+q_at_tau = q_early.subs(t, tau)
+q_late = (
+    q_at_tau * s.exp(-lam * (t - tau))
+    - U * (1 - s.exp(-lam * (t - tau))) / lam
+)
+q_integral = s.simplify(
+    s.integrate(q_early, (t, 0, tau))
+    + s.integrate(q_late, (t, tau, 2 * tau))
+)
+target_q_integral = U * (1 - s.exp(-lam * tau)) ** 2 / lam**2
+assert s.simplify(q_integral - target_q_integral) == 0
+c_ohmic = 2 * beta * a * gamma * U**2 * q_integral
+assert s.simplify(
+    c_ohmic
+    - 2 * beta * a * gamma * U**3
+    * (1 - s.exp(-lam * tau)) ** 2 / lam**2
+) == 0
+
+# A saturating sensor reports a cubic contrast from a linear field.
+F = lambda x: x / (1 + (x / Bs) ** 2)
+k_sensor = s.series(
+    (F(r * d * U) - F(-r * d * U))
+    - r * (F(d * U) - F(-d * U)),
+    U,
+    0,
+    5,
+).removeO()
+assert s.simplify(
+    k_sensor + 2 * (r**3 - r) * d**3 * U**3 / Bs**2
+) == 0
+
+print("thermal gating: exact formula and cubic amplitude contrast PASS")
+print("ohmic heating: exact pulse integral and cubic contrast PASS")
+print("sensor saturation: cubic false positive PASS")

+"""Symbolic checks for the proposed NV-read pulse-order contrast.
+
+Only checks the declared illustrative ODE and algebra. It is not experimental data.
+Run: python3 verify_order_contrast.py
+"""
+
+import sympy as s
+
+u, v, a, b, tau, r, k = s.symbols(
+    "u v a b tau r k", positive=True, real=True
+)
+x, z = s.symbols("x z", real=True)
+
+
+def field(amplitude):
+    return s.Matrix([v * amplitude * (1 - z), a * amplitude**2 - b * z])
+
+
+fp, fm = field(u), field(-u)
+# AB means +u first, -u second: final-order bracket Df_- f_+ - Df_+ f_-.
+bracket = s.simplify(fm.jacobian([x, z]) * fp - fp.jacobian([x, z]) * fm)
+assert s.simplify(bracket.subs(z, 0)) == s.Matrix([2 * a * u**3 * v, 0])
+
+# z(t) is the same in both orders, because u(t)^2 is the same.
+t = s.symbols("t", nonnegative=True, real=True)
+z_t = a * u**2 / b * (1 - s.exp(-b * t))
+first = s.integrate(v * u * (1 - z_t), (t, 0, tau))
+second = s.integrate(v * u * (1 - z_t), (t, tau, 2 * tau))
+# x_+-=first-second, x_-+=-first+second.
+contrast = s.simplify(k * 2 * (first - second))
+expected = 2 * k * v * a * u**3 / b**2 * (1 - s.exp(-b * tau)) ** 2
+assert s.simplify(contrast - expected) == 0
+assert s.simplify(s.limit(contrast / tau**2, tau, 0) - 2 * k * v * a * u**3) == 0
+
+K = s.simplify(contrast.subs(u, r * u) - r * contrast)
+assert s.simplify(K - (r**3 - r) * contrast) == 0
+
+# A purely linear relaxing local magnetic state has an order effect C~u,
+# but the amplitude contrast cancels it for any a,b,tau.
+c = s.symbols("c", real=True)
+linear_C = -2 * c * u / b * (1 - s.exp(-b * tau)) ** 2
+assert s.simplify(linear_C.subs(u, r * u) - r * linear_C) == 0
+
+print("bracket =", bracket)
+print("toy C(u,tau) =", contrast)
+print("toy K(r,u,tau) =", K)
+print("linear relaxing control K = 0")

+# A buried delamination as its own acoustic beacon and heat target
+
+**15 October 2026 (Brisbane). Status: conditional construction; operation NOT ACHIEVED. Novelty: UNKNOWN.** This is an original proposed combination and an analytic channel test, not a laboratory result or a claim that time reversal, nonlinear guide stars, or ultrasonic repair are new. No experiment or numerical simulation was run for this report.
+
+## Exact proposed operation and substrate
+
+Repair one isolated, **buried matrix delamination with intact reinforcing fibres** in a removable 2–4 mm continuous-fibre thermoplastic *test coupon*. The candidate substrate is manufactured with a thin, resin-rich, weldable interleaf at the susceptible ply boundary, plus accessible surface or edge locations for a reversible piezoelectric array and a compressive fixture. The interleaf is a deliberate material input and may affect pristine strength, mass, and fatigue life; those penalties must be measured. The panel is not an arbitrary already-built composite and the scheme cannot repair severed fibres. A coarse conventional ultrasonic C-scan can restrict the region of interest, but its acquisition is charged to both arms of the comparison.
+
+The **proposed acceptance test**, not a demonstrated specification, is that a delamination at the specified interleaf is rebonded without opening another defect or degrading the surrounding laminate, and matched post-repair Mode-I interlaminar fracture toughness reaches at least 80% of undamaged interleaf controls. The Mode-I test is destructive qualification on coupons, not a per-part certificate. A C-scan or CT indication that a gap has disappeared is insufficient: it can result from mere closure under the clamp. Measure retained compression/fatigue properties as secondary outcomes and count all failed panels. The consequential application is local repair of an enclosed bondline without opening the laminate, if a qualified nondestructive acceptance test is developed and total equipment/fabrication cost beats direct repair.
+
+## Closest incumbents, credited up front
+
+The wave-access primitive itself is established. Ulrich, Johnson and Guyer [focused processed nonlinear elastic emissions back onto a crack-like scatterer](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.98.104301) in 2007. Le Bas and colleagues [focused on an interior glass–aluminium contact used as a nonlinear scatterer](https://doi.org/10.1121/1.3638926) in 2011. Smagin and colleagues [combined a pump, a probe coda, and time reversal to detect local damage](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ultras.2020.106226) in 2020. Thus detecting a nonlinear contact, extracting a nonlinear component, and replaying it is **not** a novel mechanism by itself. A 2018 [contact-nonlinearity time-reversal analysis](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jsv.2017.12.019) also warns that narrowband retransmission does not reverse the *full* nonlinear scattering process; the present construction only reverses propagation of a selected emitted component through the approximately linear surroundings.
+
+The repair primitive is also established. Hargou and colleagues [ultrasonically activated a mendable polymer inside carbon–epoxy laminates](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.compositesb.2012.07.016) and measured Mode-I recovery, while a 2026 [delamination-repair patent application](https://patents.justia.com/patent/20260048561) reports a surface horn repairing embedded thermoplastic delaminations, with CT before/after and an example nominal weld setting of 1500 J. The patent's CT report is the applicant's evidence, not independent strength validation; its stated 1500 J weld setting is not whole-system electrical energy. Levy, Le Corre and Villegas [modelled dry-friction and bulk viscoelastic heating](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jmatprotec.2014.02.009) and found that their particular welding apparatus had 13% global efficiency; that number is not transferable to this proposed array. These are the strongest baselines and physical constraints, not minor references.
+
+## Conditional construction: same-mode sideband replay
+
+1. Couple an \(N\)-channel, phase-calibrated **shear-sensitive** array to the panel. Apply a low-amplitude carrier near a selectable guided-wave mode \(\omega\), plus a slow normal-load or acoustic dither \(\Omega\). Sweep frequency, preload, and source position inside a pre-specified region; log every probe shot and couplant condition. A contacting delamination may generate a coherent sideband at \(\omega+\Omega\). Measure phase-resolved complex array response, subtract linear electronic/acoustic backgrounds using pump-off, reversed-pump and intact controls, and test repeatability. A bulk nonlinearity, transducer nonlinearity, another crack, or a clamp contact can otherwise masquerade as an internal beacon.
+2. Select the sideband component attributed to the target interface and transmit its conjugate from the same calibrated array at **that sideband frequency and shear channel**. This is one experimentally acquired column of the Green operator; a full 3-D inverse reconstruction is not needed to form the matched focus. The phase conjugate of a harmonic at \(2\omega\) cannot simply be used for a therapeutic carrier at \(\omega\), because propagation and modal content differ. A near-carrier sideband reduces but does not remove this mismatch; driving the *same* \(\omega+\Omega\) mode is the clean construction.
+3. Raise power in short pulses while a calibrated clamp holds intimate contact. The resin-rich interleaf is intended to act as a heat director and weldable feedstock. Alternate high-power pulses with low-power sideband and linear ultrasonic readout. Reacquire the beacon whenever clamp pressure, temperature, or couplant changes enough to alter propagation. Do not interpret beacon disappearance as proof of bonding: pressure closure, thermal softening, damage growth, or loss of acoustic coupling can each suppress it.
+4. Cool under load, then inspect without preload and mechanically test blinded coupons. The operation ends in a *measured bond* only if the independent test passes.
+
+The co-obtained internal information is limited but real: the measured phase vector of a current nonlinear source and how its response changes under probe/preload. It can serve as a local action guide without Cartesian coordinates. It does **not** by itself report absolute interface temperature, frictional dissipation, polymer diffusion, strength, or even which of several contacts emitted the strongest signal. Coarse C-scan targeting, single-defect preparation, and post-repair inspection remain explicit inputs.
+
+## Original mathematical screen and decisive boundary
+
+Let \(h_a(\omega)\in\mathbb C^N\) map array drive amplitudes \(u\) to the *repair-relevant local shear displacement* \(s=h_a^T u\) at a buried interface. Let \(h_b(\omega')\) be the array vector received from the nonlinear beacon's traction mode at \(\omega'=\omega+\Omega\). Linear reciprocity in the surrounding medium means a **same-frequency, same-traction** beacon can reveal the adjoint of its own input channel. With an input norm budget \(\|u\|^2\le P\), Cauchy–Schwarz gives
+
+\[
+ |s|^2\le P\|h_a\|^2,
+ \qquad u_{\rm opt}=\sqrt P\,h_a^*/\|h_a\|.
+\]
+
+If instead \(u=\sqrt P\,h_b^*/\|h_b\|\) is made from the observed sideband, the fraction of this maximum local shear intensity is
+
+\[
+ \eta=\frac{|h_a^T h_b^*|^2}{\|h_a\|^2\|h_b\|^2}\in[0,1].
+\]
+
+This is a **necessary channel-alignment test** for the promised action. Strong, clean beacon SNR alone puts no lower bound on \(\eta\). For two channels, a normal-symmetric beacon vector \(h_b=(1,1)/\sqrt2\) and an antisymmetric shear-heating vector \(h_a=(1,-1)/\sqrt2\) give \(\eta=0\), despite both being perfectly observable/controllable. This is a mathematical counterexample to the claim that *any* internal nonlinear guide star automatically provides the control mode needed for repair. The intended rescue is same-mode sideband emission and matched shear reception/actuation; actual composites may still mix modes or change under load. Neither \(h_a\) nor \(\eta\) was measured here.
+
+An independent thermal gate follows. Write \(K''\) for the loss component of the interleaf's *patch stiffness*, \(\delta\) for its shear displacement, \(F_t\) for total frictional shear force, and \(f=\omega/(2\pi)\). A schematic cycle-averaged input is \(P_{\rm int}\simeq\tfrac12\omega K''(T,p)|\delta|^2+f\!\oint F_t\,d\delta\), from interleaf viscoelastic loss and interfacial slip, while surrounding resin/fibres dissipate \(P_{\rm bulk}\simeq\int_V\tfrac12\omega\,\epsilon:C''\epsilon\,dV\). This is a bookkeeping split, not a fitted constitutive law, and overlapping losses must not be double-counted. Successful focusing of shear is insufficient unless integrated interface heat supplies the melt/softening enthalpy and bond dwell time **before** off-target bulk heating or fibre/matrix damage. At least \(E_{\rm int}\ge m_{\rm weld}[c_p(T_{\rm weld}-T_0)+L_{\rm eff}]\) is needed in an idealized thermal budget, plus conduction loss and hold/cooling; all parameters must be measured for the chosen interleaf. Conventional thermoplastic welding often uses 20–40 kHz vibration in the inspected [CF/PEEK study](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S1526612518304821). For an *illustrative, unmeasured* guided-mode phase speed of 3000 m/s, 40 kHz gives \(\lambda=75\) mm, much wider than a 5–15 mm defect. A sub-wavelength nonlinear beacon does not make the *actuation field* sub-wavelength. Heat could still localize through interleaf loss, but this is the unproven part; moving to higher frequency trades spatial selectivity against attenuation and available power.
+
+There is also an **identifiability obstruction**: a reactive contact nonlinearity can create the same sideband as a lossy slipping contact while dissipating much less heat. Mathematically, the sideband measures a nonlinear scattering coefficient/derivative, whereas heat depends on loss modulus and hysteresis area. Distinct pairs \(K'(\delta,p),K''(T,p)\) can have the same low-power sideband but different \(P_{\rm int}\) and final bond strength. Hence the sideband cannot independently certify the thermal dose or completed weld. This rules out promoting a beacon-only closed loop as operational closure; the redesign uses the same beacon **for aiming**, an independently calibrated energy/temperature window for actuation, and independent outcome tests.
+
+## Why optical and bubble guide stars do not fill the missing interface
+
+Acoustically induced bubble emissions were already [time-reversed through an excised human skull to improve a therapy focus](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3081822/) in a phantom experiment; the authors first used CT-derived focusing to create the bubble. [TRUME optical focusing](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4673873/) used selective microbubble destruction and optical phase conjugation to focus light at a bubble in a scattering phantom. These are concrete demonstrations of conditional internal guide stars, and they also show the preparation cost of creating/selecting the beacon. For a carbon-fibre laminate, an optical playback path through the opaque load-bearing plies and a mobile microbubble at the *dry* bondline are not available assumptions. Seeding a bubble would alter the bond and count as new material preparation. The acoustic contact beacon is the physically closer route for this substrate. For tissue applications the bubble methods are strong incumbents, so moving the same idea there would not establish novelty.
+
+## Full-cost matched comparison
+
+The comparator is **C-scan localisation plus a calibrated conventional ultrasonic horn under the same fixture and on the same interleaf substrate**, with oven/resistance repair admitted if a horn cannot access the site. It gets the same pre/post inspection, acceptance rule, measured electricity, set-up time, and rejected coupons. The patent gives a concrete horn baseline with reported CT closure; the 2013 polymer study gives mechanical-strength evidence, although on a different laminate. No advantage follows from array pulse energy alone.
+
+| Resource or risk | Beacon/time-reversal candidate | Strong conventional comparator |
+|---|---|---|
+| Substrate and preparation | Resin-rich interleaf; array attachment/couplant; clamp; possible permanently installed channels; pristine mechanical penalty | Same interleaf and clamp for matched comparison; horn couplant/support or oven/blanket |
+| Information acquired | Coarse C-scan, nonlinear sideband sweeps, phase calibration, rejection of equipment/clamp nonlinearity, remeasurement after each geometry/temperature change | C-scan and registration to horn; process-window calibration and post-repair inspection |
+| Actuation and heat | \(N\) power amplifiers, beamforming, pulse energy, cooling, bulk attenuation and unwanted focus/sidelobes; true wall-plug energy unknown | Horn generator and pressure fixture, or whole-part oven/resistance energy; measured rather than nominal settings |
+| Reliability and verification | Beacon failures, multiple sources, mode mismatch, delamination that becomes acoustically silent, heating/couplant drift, destructive strength coupons or qualified NDT | Registration error, horn footprint/access limits, off-target heat, incomplete fusion/overheating, identical qualification tests |
+| Scaling | Repeated scans/recalibration per flaw; fixed array may amortize only over enough panels | Horn/oven fixture time and repositioning per flaw; can process many similar panels |
+
+The 2026 horn patent example describes 1500 J nominal weld energy and seconds of sonication/hold with CT-reported gap disappearance, but supplies no matched input electricity or Mode-I comparison to this candidate. The 2014 13% global-efficiency number applies to its own modelled apparatus only. Thus **no full-cost or performance advantage is established**.
+
+## Decisive experiment and status gate
+
+Make a pre-registered randomized set of otherwise identical laminates with one blind, buried delamination at the interleaf, plus intact, open-gap and deliberately linear-scatterer controls. Hold the conventional C-scan, operator information, clamp, substrate, and outcome tests equal. First, verify that the sideband persists at the *actual welding preload* and originates at the intended defect rather than array/clamp contacts. In instrumented sacrificial coupons, measure interface shear displacement and mode content under beacon replay versus a directly calibrated optimal drive to estimate \(\eta\); separate calibration coupons are necessary because embedded sensors can themselves change an interface. Map interface and bulk temperature/heat-affected zones with calibrated witness sensors and sectioning, record wall-plug energy and elapsed time, then test healed Mode-I toughness blinded after unloading. Repeat across flaw sizes, depths, fibre directions, and couplant resets. Compare against C-scan-plus-horn and, where relevant, oven repair under the same acceptance rule.
+
+The candidate should be **parked** if the beacon is absent under bond-forming preload, \(\eta\) is too small for an attainable interface heat dose, bulk damage occurs before weld formation, or bonded strength/full-system cost fails to beat the incumbent. If these pass, novelty still requires a separate detailed prior-art and patent review. Nothing here establishes a repair, a cost saving, or a new time-reversal principle.
+
+## Source inspection and provenance
+
+Primary source pages and abstracts/previews actually inspected on 15 October 2026 (not a full-text systematic review): [Ulrich et al. 2007 PRL abstract](https://journals.aps.org/prl/abstract/10.1103/PhysRevLett.98.104301) (nonlinear response extracted and replayed onto a scatterer); [Le Bas et al. 2011 author-institution search-indexed paper extract](https://physics.byu.edu/docs/publication/1555) and [article DOI/abstract](https://doi.org/10.1121/1.3638926) (interior glass–aluminium contact beacon; direct institutional page later redirected to login); [Smagin et al. 2020 article preview](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0041624X20301657) (pump/probe coda and time reversal); [2018 contact-nonlinearity article preview](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0022460X17308726) (full-spectrum versus narrowband reversal); [Hargou et al. 2013 abstract/preview](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1359836812004477) (EMAA ultrasonic repair and Mode-I test); [Levy et al. 2014 article preview](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0924013614000508) (friction and bulk-loss heating model, apparatus efficiency); [Wang et al. 2019 welding article preview](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S1526612518304821) (CF/PEEK under- and over-weld regimes); [2026 delamination repair patent full description and worked examples](https://patents.justia.com/patent/20260048561) (embedded defect, horn load/energy settings, CT); [2009 bubble time-reversal search-indexed paper text/abstract](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3081822/) (skull phantom focusing with a bubble); [2015 TRUME search-indexed paper text/abstract](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4673873/) (bubble-destruction optical guide star). The two equations for channel alignment and the sideband-versus-heat obstruction above are **original derivations/arguments**, not claims taken from these sources. Search snippets exposed some paper text where publisher pages later returned access errors; any result beyond that exposed text remains uninspected.
