+# Independent audit: hidden dissipation from three passive observations
+
+**Date:** 15 October 2026. **Status:** mathematical derivation independently checked below; no laboratory observation, peer review, or exhaustive novelty assessment. This follow-up audits the root's geometric-mean argument and records the earlier, weaker reversibilization check. It does not identify the exact all-architecture optimum or an attaining model.
+
+## Result and quantifiers
+
+Let \(Q\) be **any finite irreducible stationary CTMC generator** in row convention, with stationary law \(\pi\), all microscopic variables even under ordinary time reversal, and a deterministic observation \(Y=h(X)\). Let \(B\) be one observed label, \(p=\Pr(Y_0=B)>0\), and for a fixed \(t>0\) define
+
+\[
+ a=a_t=\Pr(Y_t=B\mid Y_0=B)=\Pr(Y_{-t}=B\mid Y_0=B),\quad
+ b=b_t=\Pr(Y_{-t}=B,Y_t=B\mid Y_0=B),\quad
+ D=p(a^2-b).
+\]
+
+If \(0<a<1\) and \(D>0\), then every exact realization with finite entropy-production rate \(\sigma(Q)\) obeys \(D<a(1-a)\) and
+
+\[
+ \boxed{\displaystyle \sigma(Q)\ \geq\ -\frac1t\log\left(1-\frac{D}{a(1-a)}\right).}\tag{1}
+\]
+
+The centering \(a\) in (1) is convenient but not optimal. Put \(w_{00}=1-2a+b\), \(w_{01}=a-b=w_{10}\), and \(w_{11}=b\). If these cells are positive and \(b<a^2\), then \(w_{01}>\sqrt{w_{00}w_{11}}\), and a stronger certificate is
+
+\[
+ \boxed{\displaystyle
+ \sigma(Q)\geq-\frac1t\log(1-C_t),\qquad
+ C_t=2p\bigl(w_{01}-\sqrt{w_{00}w_{11}}\bigr)>0.}\tag{1*}
+\]
+
+Boundary cells are treated by a one-sided limit. The claim is **uniform in hidden dimension and hidden rates**, and needs only the observed three-time law. It does not require an alternating-renewal target. If \(\sigma(Q)=+\infty\), the lower bounds are vacuous. Any finite-cost exact realization forces \(C_t<1\).
+
+For the target \(P_q\) observed from the three-state ring of the primary sources, \(q\in(0,1)\), \(p=2/3\), \(s=1+q\), and the result implies
+
+\[
+ \boxed{\displaystyle V_\infty(P_q)\geq\frac23(1-\sqrt q)^2}.\tag{2}
+\]
+
+In particular, \(V_\infty(P_{1/20})\geq(21-4\sqrt5)/30\approx0.4018576030>2/5\), since \(9>4\sqrt5\). These are target inverse-time units with \(k_B=1\). This improves the **previously released candidate lower certificate** \(V_\infty(P_{1/20})>0.017568198744\), but is well below the ring realization's cost \((19/20)\log20\approx2.84595\). Neither number locates the optimum or settles attainment.
+
+## Proof audit: the geometric path measure
+
+Write \(Q^*=D_\pi^{-1}Q^{\mathsf T}D_\pi\) for the stationary reverse and consider the microscopic path laws \(P=P_Q^{[-t,t]}\) and \(P^*=P_{Q^*}^{[-t,t]}\). Both start with \(\pi\) at the left endpoint. Stationarity gives \(Q^*_{ii}=Q_{ii}\). If a positive edge has no reverse, \(\sigma(Q)=+\infty\); the rest of this proof assumes finite cost, so the path laws have mutual support.
+
+For any common dominating path measure, define \(\mu=(P+P^*)/2\) and the **subprobability** \(\nu\) with density \(\sqrt{dP\,dP^*}\). Arithmetic-geometric mean gives \(\mu-\nu\geq0\) as a measure, with total mass \(1-A\), where \(A=\int\sqrt{dP\,dP^*}\) is the path Hellinger affinity. This is an inequality between path measures; \(\mu\) is not the path law of the additive reversibilization.
+
+The product-of-jump-rates path density shows that \(\nu\) has initial law \(\pi\) and a killed generator \(G\) with
+
+\[
+ G_{ij}=\sqrt{Q_{ij}Q^*_{ij}}\quad(i\ne j),\qquad G_{ii}=Q_{ii}.
+\]
+
+The holding-time factors combine without an extra potential because \(Q_{ii}=Q^*_{ii}\). Its row sums are nonpositive by arithmetic-geometric mean. Moreover \(\pi_iG_{ij}=\sqrt{\pi_i\pi_jQ_{ij}Q_{ji}}=\pi_jG_{ji}\), so \(G\) is self-adjoint in \(L^2(\pi)\). Killing, rather than normalizing, is essential: normalization would generally destroy this simple path formula.
+
+Fix \(f=1_B-a\mathbf1\) and the symmetric path score
+
+\[
+ W=1_B(X_0)f(X_{-t})f(X_t).
+\]
+
+Reversal swaps the endpoints and leaves \(W\) unchanged, hence \(E_\mu W=E_PW=-D\). For the geometric submeasure, the killed Markov composition and self-adjointness give the exact nonnegative square
+
+\[
+ E_\nu W
+ =\sum_i\pi_i1_B(i)\,[e^{tG}f(i)]^2\geq0.\tag{3}
+\]
+
+Because the three factors are binary-centered, \(W\geq-a(1-a)\) pathwise. Therefore
+
+\[
+ -D=E_\nu W+E_{\mu-\nu}W\geq-a(1-a)(1-A),
+ \qquad D\leq a(1-a)(1-A).\tag{4}
+\]
+
+The full-path relative entropy is \(D_{\mathrm{KL}}(P\Vert P^*)=2t\sigma(Q)\): stationarity removes boundary entropy and the same holding rates cancel in the likelihood ratio. Jensen applied to \(A=E_P\exp[-\tfrac12\log(dP/dP^*)]\) yields \(A\geq\exp[-t\sigma(Q)]\). Combining with (4) yields \(D\leq a(1-a)(1-e^{-t\sigma})\), and rearranging proves (1). **The direction of both inequalities is as needed**: replacing \(A\) by its lower bound makes the allowed deficit larger, not smaller.
+
+The same proof works with **any** score center \(r\in(0,1)\): put \(f_r=1_B-r\mathbf1\), \(W_r=1_B(X_0)f_r(X_{-t})f_r(X_t)\), and \(D_r=-E_QW_r=p[\delta-(a-r)^2]\), where \(\delta=a^2-b\). If \(D_r>0\), then \(\sigma\geq-t^{-1}\log[1-D_r/\{r(1-r)\}]\). To optimize this ratio, set \(z=r/(1-r)>0\). A direct expansion of the four conditional endpoint cells gives
+
+\[
+ \frac{D_r}{r(1-r)}
+ =p\left[2w_{01}-w_{00}z-\frac{w_{11}}z\right]
+ \leq 2p\left(w_{01}-\sqrt{w_{00}w_{11}}\right)=C_t.
+\]
+
+Equality holds at \(z=\sqrt{w_{11}/w_{00}}\), equivalently \(r=\sqrt{w_{11}}/(\sqrt{w_{11}}+\sqrt{w_{00}})\). This proves (1*); \(w_{01}^2-w_{00}w_{11}=a^2-b>0\) proves its positivity. The optimized inequality is a new derivation in this audit, not an optimum over all possible observable scores.
+
+The proof requires the usual finite-state, stationary, noninvasive deterministic observation model. It does not apply as written to odd-parity microscopic reversal, time-dependent generators, causal measurements that alter \(Q\), or arbitrary temporally correlated observation noise.
+
+## Exact ring calculation and independent checks
+
+For
+
+\[
+ Q_q=\begin{pmatrix}-s&1&q\\q&-s&1\\1&q&-s\end{pmatrix},\quad
+ \pi=(1/3,1/3,1/3),\quad h(0)=A,\ h(1)=h(2)=B,
+\]
+
+put \(\gamma=3s/2\) and \(\omega=\sqrt3(1-q)/2\). Conditional on \(X_0=1\) or \(2\), the future \(B\)-success probabilities are
+
+\[
+ u(t)=\frac23+e^{-\gamma t}\left(\frac{\cos(\omega t)}3+\frac{\sin(\omega t)}{\sqrt3}\right),\qquad
+ v(t)=\frac23+e^{-\gamma t}\left(\frac{\cos(\omega t)}3-\frac{\sin(\omega t)}{\sqrt3}\right).
+\]
+
+The past probabilities swap \(u,v\). Consequently \(a=(u+v)/2=2/3+e^{-\gamma t}\cos(\omega t)/3\), \(b=uv\), and
+
+\[
+ a^2-b=\frac13e^{-3st}\sin^2(\omega t)>0
+ \quad\text{for }\sin(\omega t)\ne0.\tag{5}
+\]
+
+As \(t\downarrow0\), \(a=1-st/2+O(t^2)\), \(w_{01}=st/2+O(t^2)\), \(w_{00}=qt^2+O(t^3)\), and \(w_{11}=1+O(t)\). Hence \(C_t/t\to p(s-2\sqrt q)=\frac23(1-\sqrt q)^2\), proving (2). The unoptimized right side of (1) tends to \((1-q)^2/[3(1+q)]\), equal to \(361/1260\) at \(q=1/20\). For **each** finite exact realization the finite-\(t\) inequality holds for every sufficiently small \(t\); taking this target-law limit before the infimum over hidden realizations creates no hidden uniform-rate assumption.
+
+At \(q=1/20,t=3/10\), an independent 60-digit matrix-exponential check gave \(a=0.8681827585774305281\ldots\), \(E_QW=-D=-0.00515576738019247919\ldots\), \(E_\nu W=0.00234432217129927112\ldots\), \(A=0.6965108954780772159\ldots\), and \(a(1-a)(1-A)=0.0347317350885180571\ldots\). Formula (1) gives \(0.15365980295790974\ldots\); optimizing the center via (1*) gives \(0.17033643656648687\ldots\). These numerics check the signs and factors; the exact small-time constant follows from the algebra above, not from floating point. The scripts high_precision_geometric_check.py and audit_calculations.py in this worker directory reproduce the checks; neither certifies a global optimum.
+
+## Independently checked jitter and stochastic-readout extension
+
+The square argument survives **independent identically distributed** left and right sampling gaps \(T_-,T_+\sim\rho\), independent of the CTMC, with finite common mean \(m>0\). It also survives a fixed, passive, memoryless binary readout: at each sampled time, conditional on microscopic state \(i\), independently draw \(Z\in\{0,1\}\) with \(\Pr(Z=1\mid X=i)=b_i\in[0,1]\). Choose any score center \(r\in(0,1)\), for example the common conditional endpoint marginal \(\Pr(Z_{T_+}=1\mid Z_0=1)=\Pr(Z_{-T_-}=1\mid Z_0=1)\), whose equality follows from stationarity when the same channel is used at all three times, and let
+
+\[
+ W=Z_0(Z_{-T_-}-r)(Z_{T_+}-r),\qquad D=-E_Q W>0.
+\]
+
+The common gap distribution and endpoint channel make the joint observation protocol invariant under time reversal. Attach its common clock and sensor kernel to \(P\) and \(P^*\); their geometric mean retains that kernel. With \(f=b-r\mathbf1\), integrating the iid gaps in the killed path law gives
+
+\[
+ E_\nu W=\sum_i\pi_i b_i\left[ E_{T\sim\rho}(e^{TG}f)(i)\right]^2\geq0.\tag{6}
+\]
+
+Because \(W\geq-r(1-r)\), (4) holds with \(a\) replaced by \(r\). Conditional path affinity over a total length \(T_-+T_+\) is at least \(e^{-\sigma(T_-+T_+)/2}\); averaging and Jensen give \(A\geq e^{-m\sigma}\). Hence
+
+\[
+ \boxed{\displaystyle \sigma(Q)\geq-\frac1m\log\left(1-\frac{D}{r(1-r)}\right).}\tag{7}
+\]
+
+The center channel may be a different fixed Bernoulli kernel \(c_i\); then the factor \(b_i\) outside the square in (6) becomes \(c_i\). Keep \(r\) as any chosen scalar and compute \(D=-E_QW\) directly: with distinct center and endpoint kernels, the two conditional endpoint marginals need not coincide under a nonreversible chain. Equal *endpoint* kernels and identically distributed independent gaps remain the relevant conditions. A common passive sensor at three times is the most direct physical interpretation. Unequal or correlated gaps, state-dependent clock selection, temporally correlated readout errors, and measurement disturbance need separate analysis; (6) must not be silently applied to them. Random jitter needs its actual distribution or a justified uncertainty set; the theorem is not an empirical calibration of clocks or sensors.
+
+If the conditional endpoint cells given \(Z_0=1\) are now \(w_{uv}\), possibly with \(w_{01}\ne w_{10}\), the same one-dimensional optimization gives the observable coefficient \(C=p_0[(w_{01}+w_{10})-2\sqrt{w_{00}w_{11}}]\). If \(C>0\), (7) holds with its logarithm argument \(1-C\). This formula does not assume equal conditional endpoint marginals; it only uses the reversal-symmetric score and protocol.
+
+An independently executed floating fixture for \(P_{1/20}\), with iid gaps taking \(0.2\) or \(0.4\) with equal probability (\(m=0.3\)), illustrates the scope. Ideal three-time readout gives \(r=0.870657154122\ldots\), \(D=0.004726050508\ldots\), and bound \(0.142910468104\ldots\). With independent symmetric \(10\%\) errors at **all three** times, \(D=-0.004846820337\ldots\), so this score gives no positive certificate even though the theorem remains true. If only the endpoints have that error and the center is ideal, \(D=0.003024672325\ldots\) and the bound is \(0.062796021825\ldots\). These are model calculations, not measured sensor performance.
+
+## Earlier additive-reversibilization certificate: valid but superseded here
+
+The 3 October candidate release already proves the path comparison for \(R=(Q+Q^*)/2\): \(D_{\rm KL}(P_Q^{[0,T]}\Vert P_R^{[0,T]})\leq T\sigma(Q)/4\). The killed \(R_B\) is self-adjoint and negative, so its no-exit \(B\)-persistence \(H_R(t)\) is completely monotone. If the target's third finite difference \(d_h=H(3h)-3H(2h)+3H(h)-H(0)>0\), the nested event score takes values \(-1,0,2\), with range width 3; Pinsker on \(T=3h\) then gives the valid but weak certificate \(\sigma\geq8d_h^2/(27h)\). For \(q=1/20\), \(H'''(0)=2387/8000>0\), so positive \(d_h\) exists for small \(h\). A floating grid of \(h=0.001,\ldots,10\) gave a best displayed value \(1.0197\times10^{-5}\) at \(h=0.419\), **not** a certified optimum. Squaring a negative \(d_h\) would be invalid. This route is substantially weaker than both (2) and the candidate release's fixed-window certificate.
+
+For a more operational comparison, the candidate release's fixed-window result requires continuous no-exit observation on both sides. The new bound (1) uses only three passive snapshots, though a near-zero-time implementation would demand increasing temporal resolution and statistical precision. Its negative score is \(O(t^2)\) while \(1-a=O(t)\); a distribution-free Hoeffding calculation for independent bounded triplet scores and a \(t^2\) absolute margin scales as \(t^{-4}\) replicates. Target-specific variance and structured estimation may improve that scaling, and repeated samples from one trajectory require dependence/mixing analysis. Infinite precision at arbitrarily small \(t\) is a property of the **exact target law**, not an experimentally established affordance. At any fixed \(t>0\), (1) remains a finite-window certificate with a finite, weaker constant.
+
+## Prior art and status
+
+The original [thermodynamic-realizability preprint](https://arxiv.org/html/2609.14623) conjectures zero all-dimension cost in §6 and calculates a positive dwell-density slope in §8.8. A later, unreviewed [Evidence Press release](https://www.evidencepress.org/releases/hidden-dissipation-floor/) and its [full source](https://github.com/ipitchford/hidden-dissipation-floor/blob/main/PAPER.tex) already refute zero cost under the finite stationary even-variable assumptions, supply the additive-reversibilization path inequality and a stronger qualitative zero-cost classification, and explicitly leave the positive optimum and attainment open. The geometric-mean proof above is an independently audited improvement to the *numerical lower certificate and sampling access*, not a first refutation of the conjecture. A targeted reading of that release found no Hellinger/geometric-mean path construction, but wider prior art for this exact bound is **UNKNOWN**. Geometric rate symmetrizations are themselves established; see [Choi and Wolfer, Systematic Approaches to Generate Reversiblizations of Markov Chains](https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.03650). Their conservative reversiblizations should not be conflated with the killed geometric path measure used here. General thermodynamic inference from coarse observations predates both works; see, for example, the primary [Nature Communications study on broken detailed balance without observable currents](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-019-11051-w).
+
+The decisive remaining tests are (i) independent specialist proof review of the geometric-submeasure identification and the small-time quantifier; (ii) a systematic primary-literature search for equivalent Hellinger/path-affinity lower bounds; and (iii) a finite-rate, sampled-readout study with calibrated jitter/noise and valid confidence intervals, comparing (7) against matched existing estimators. None has been completed here.

+# Decision-theory line: live response closure
+
+15 October 2026, Australia/Brisbane. **Status: scoped exact theorem and obstruction; no established new capability.** This report concerns one live substrate, an adaptive probe protocol followed by one terminal control choice. It does not assert that arbitrary scientific control problems have been closed. The proposed operation is to measure the *joint* response of a probe and a subsequent control, including probe-induced loss of the substrate, and synthesize the control directly from that response. Mechanism identification is unnecessary **if** the relevant world-conditioned response experiments can actually be acquired. That access is the central unproved physical assumption.
+
+## Exact response theorem
+
+Let the possible mechanisms or prepared conditions be a finite set `Theta`, the probe transcript a finite set `Y`, and terminal controls a finite set `C`. Fix an admissible, possibly adaptive probe protocol `sigma` that acts on a physical substrate before the terminal control. For every `theta in Theta`, `y in Y`, `c in C`, define the **interventional response mass**
+
+```
+p[theta,y,c] = P_theta{probe transcript is y AND verified goal is reached
+                       without forbidden failure when c is applied after y}.
+```
+
+The probability includes all effects of the probe on the substrate. If the probe destroys the only viable object, its mass is zero for every terminal control on that outcome. A terminal rule is a stochastic kernel `d(c|y)` chosen only from the observed transcript. Its worst-world success probability is
+
+```
+V_sigma = max_d min_theta sum_y sum_c d(c|y) p[theta,y,c]
+          = min_{lambda in Delta(Theta)} sum_y max_c
+                sum_theta lambda(theta) p[theta,y,c].                 (1)
+```
+
+Thus a target success threshold `tau` is achievable in this two-phase interface under a resource constraint `C(sigma) <= B` exactly when some admissible `sigma` with that cost has `V_sigma >= tau`. The response tensor is task-relative: it need not specify latent states, reaction pathways, or the probability of observations that cannot lead to success. This is an *exact characterization given the tensor*, not an efficient way to discover the tensor or `sigma`.
+
+**Proof.** Condition on the probe transcript. Causal ordering gives success in world `theta` as the first linear expression in (1). Maximizing its minimum over finite stochastic terminal rules is a finite linear program. Replace the minimum over `theta` by a minimum over distributions `lambda` on `Theta`. The rule and `lambda` range over compact convex simplexes, so finite minimax swaps max and min. For fixed `lambda`, the optimizing rule independently chooses, at each `y`, a control attaining the displayed maximum. This proves (1), including randomized terminal choices and unequal world-specific probe survival. No Markov or stationarity assumption is used; all earlier adaptive probe actions are bundled into `sigma`.
+
+For two symmetric worlds with terminal controls `c0,c1` that succeed only when their indices match the world, let `mu_theta(y)=P_theta{Y=y AND substrate survives the probe}`. Equation (1) reduces to equal-prior success
+
+```
+V_sigma = (1/2) sum_y max{mu_0(y), mu_1(y)}
+        = (s_0+s_1+||mu_0-mu_1||_1)/4,                         (2)
+```
+
+provided the symmetry makes equal prior least favorable; otherwise the minimization in (1), not (2), gives the minimax value. Here `s_theta=sum_y mu_theta(y)`. Formula (2) is a **live-information** measure: a perfectly informative observation can be worthless when the probe has removed the ability to act.
+
+## Decisive counterexample and redesign
+
+Two worlds `theta=0,1` have indistinguishable starting observations. On a live object, `c_theta` achieves the goal and the other control irreversibly fails. Without probing, randomized commitment has exact uniform success `1/2`. A proposed probe reveals `theta` perfectly, but consumes the unique object with probability `3/5`, independently of `theta`; the readout is still available when the object is lost. Its surviving response masses are `p[theta,theta,c_theta]=2/5`, all other success masses zero. Equation (1) gives `V_probe=2/5`: *perfect mechanism identification makes control worse* than acting without the probe. The failure is physical viability, not information access.
+
+A substantive redesign is a protected probe that preserves the object with probability `9/10` and, conditional on survival, reports the wrong world with probability `1/10`. The matching-control rule then has exact uniform success `(9/10)(9/10)=81/100`; (1) certifies this value. The redesigned probe beats the `1/2` no-probe policy only when `s(1-e)>1/2` in this symmetric binary fixture. This threshold includes both information quality and material survival. **These are constructed probabilities, not measured properties of a device.** A useful physical instantiation would need a readout that actually achieves the claimed `s,e` and leaves the actuator compatible with the object.
+
+The same algebra admits a probe that reveals nothing but improves the object: if an observation-independent preparation increases the success mass of a universal terminal control from `2/5` to `4/5` in both worlds, operational value doubles while statistical informativeness is unchanged. That is why the joint probe/control response, rather than a sensor-only order, is the quantity to acquire.
+
+## How a direct certificate could be acquired, and its limits
+
+Suppose each `theta` can be *independently prepared or unambiguously stratified* into fresh, exchangeable specimens, the probe `sigma` and every `c` can be executed on each specimen, and goal/failure can be verified. For each `(theta,c)`, perform `n` independent runs of `sigma` followed by `c` regardless of `y`; record each transcript and success. The empirical frequency of `{Y=y AND success}` estimates `p[theta,y,c]`. With `M=|Theta|`, `K=|C|`, `J=|Y|`, Hoeffding plus a union bound gives simultaneous cell error at most
+
+```
+r = sqrt(log(2 M K J / delta)/(2 n))
+```
+
+with probability at least `1-delta`. Solve (1) with lower masses `L[theta,y,c]=max(0,p_hat[theta,y,c]-r)`. The attained rule then has true worst-world success at least `V(L)` on that confidence event. Also `V(L) >= V(p)-2 J r`; hence `n >= 2 J^2 log(2 M K J/delta)/epsilon^2` suffices to lose at most `epsilon` in certified value relative to the best terminal rule for *this fixed probe*. These bounds are elementary and conservative. They charge `M K n` complete sacrificial trials, including preparation, probing, terminal actuation, and verification; the formula does not price energy, duration, disposal, or creating known-`theta` specimens. Search over probe protocols is an additional cost and can be exponential in horizon and branching.
+
+If there is only one irreplaceable substrate, if `theta` cannot be prepared/stratified, or if repeated trials alter the response law, the finite-sample certificate is unavailable. Testing only the deployment mixture certifies its mixture success, not a uniform guarantee over worlds. One can instead evaluate complete closed-loop policies directly on independently reset copies; an equally informed comparator can do that and may be cheaper than tensor estimation. The theorem creates no free experimental access.
+
+## Prior art and comparator boundary
+
+This report's proof and examples are original derivations for the stated fixture, but the minimax LP is classical decision theory; **novelty is UNKNOWN and should not be claimed**. Blackwell's experiment comparison concerns information available for a decision under a fixed downstream decision problem. Here the probe changes the physical opportunity for that decision, so the response masses must include survival and post-probe control effects. That observation is consistent with established dual control, not a displacement of it. [Blackwell, *Equivalent Comparisons of Experiments* (1953), DOI](https://doi.org/10.1214/aoms/1177729032) was checked at the journal landing page/metadata; the full original PDF was not accessible in this browse. [Feldbaum, *On a class of dual control learning systems* (1964)](https://www.mathnet.ru/eng/at11622) explicitly describes trial actions of cognitive nature combined with actions that bring a plant to the required state; the archive abstract was inspected, not the Russian full text.
+
+Most importantly, merely stopping when all surviving mechanisms share a successful decision is already [Javdani et al., *Near Optimal Bayesian Active Learning for Decision Making* (AISTATS 2014)](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v33/javdani14.pdf): its Section 2 states the version-space-in-one-overlapping-decision-region criterion and Section 3 gives hyperedge cutting. Dynamic belief-support reach-avoid synthesis and antichains are also established; [Chatterjee et al., *Games with Imperfect Information: Theory and Algorithms*](https://lsv.ens-paris-saclay.fr/~doyen/papers/Games_with_Imperfect_Information_Theory_Algorithms.pdf), Sections 3.1–3.4, gives knowledge-set updates, winning constructions, and rank/strategy issues. [Junges, Jansen and Seshia, *Enforcing Almost-Sure Reachability in POMDPs*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2007.00085) explicitly targets safe winning regions. These are the strongest equally informed planning comparators; given the same acquired response data or a full model, they can represent the same decision problem. No computation, sample, energy, or reliability advantage is demonstrated here.
+
+The next decisive test is on a real, single-use control substrate with two or more plausible hidden conditions. Specify goal/failure and the best no-probe and POMDP/dual-control policies **before** testing. Measure the world-stratified joint success tensor of a genuinely viability-preserving probe and terminal actions on matched specimens, with preparation and attrition fully charged; then prospectively deploy the LP rule on fresh blinded specimens. The probe has value only if the lower confidence bound on its worst-world success exceeds the matched comparator after total resource accounting. No such substrate or experiment was available in this investigation.

+"""Exploratory floating-point checks for FOLLOWUP_DISSIPATION_AUDIT.md.
+
+The analytic statements are proved in the report. Grid maxima printed here are
+diagnostics, not certified global optima or empirical measurements.
+"""
+
+import math
+from fractions import Fraction
+
+
+q = 1 / 20
+s = 1 + q
+omega = math.sqrt(3) * (1 - q) / 2
+gamma = 3 * s / 2
+p = 2 / 3
+
+
+def persistence(t):
+    root = math.sqrt(q)
+    return p * math.exp(-s * t) * (
+        math.cosh(root * t) + s * math.sinh(root * t) / (2 * root)
+    )
+
+
+def third_difference(h):
+    return persistence(3 * h) - 3 * persistence(2 * h) + 3 * persistence(h) - p
+
+
+def fd_bound(h):
+    d = third_difference(h)
+    return 8 * d * d / (27 * h) if d > 0 else 0.0
+
+
+def conditional_snapshot_bound(t):
+    e = math.exp(-gamma * t)
+    a = 2 / 3 + e * math.cos(omega * t) / 3
+    delta = e * e * math.sin(omega * t) ** 2 / 3
+    b = a * a - delta
+    w = ((1 - a) ** 2 - delta, a * (1 - a) + delta,
+         a * (1 - a) + delta, b)
+    independent = ((1 - a) ** 2, a * (1 - a),
+                   a * (1 - a), a * a)
+    assert min(w) >= -1e-12
+    info = sum(x * math.log(x / y) for x, y in zip(w, independent) if x > 0)
+    return 2 * p * info / t, delta
+
+
+def two_snapshot_bound(t, symmetric_error=0.0):
+    covariance = (2 / 9) * math.exp(-gamma * t) * math.cos(omega * t)
+    recorded_covariance = (1 - 2 * symmetric_error) ** 2 * covariance
+    return (8 * recorded_covariance ** 2 / t if recorded_covariance < 0 else 0.0,
+            recorded_covariance)
+
+
+def geometric_path_bound(t):
+    """New independent diagnostic; proof and exact small-time limit are in audit."""
+    e = math.exp(-gamma * t)
+    a = 2 / 3 + e * math.cos(omega * t) / 3
+    delta = e * e * math.sin(omega * t) ** 2 / 3
+    d = p * delta
+    ratio = d / (a * (1 - a))
+    return -math.log1p(-ratio) / t, a, delta, d, ratio
+
+
+def optimized_geometric_path_bound(t):
+    """Optimize the centered endpoint score over r in (0,1)."""
+    _, a, delta, _, _ = geometric_path_bound(t)
+    w11 = a * a - delta
+    w00 = 1 - 2 * a + w11
+    w01 = a - w11
+    r_star = math.sqrt(w11) / (math.sqrt(w11) + math.sqrt(w00))
+    c = 2 * p * (w01 - math.sqrt(w00 * w11))
+    return -math.log1p(-c) / t, r_star, c
+
+
+def ring_geometric_submeasure_check(t):
+    """Closed-form check of killed G for the symmetric three-state ring."""
+    _, a, _, d, _ = geometric_path_bound(t)
+    lam_0 = -s + 2 * math.sqrt(q)
+    lam_perp = -s - math.sqrt(q)
+    affinity = math.exp(2 * t * lam_0)
+    e_nu_w = p * (
+        math.exp(t * lam_0) * (p - a)
+        + math.exp(t * lam_perp) / 3
+    ) ** 2
+    return -d, e_nu_w, affinity, a * (1 - a) * (1 - affinity)
+
+
+def transition_matrix(t):
+    """Circulant three-state ring transition matrix from Fourier eigenvalues."""
+    e = math.exp(-gamma * t)
+    phases = (0.0, -2 * math.pi / 3, 2 * math.pi / 3)
+    return [[1 / 3 + 2 * e * math.cos(omega * t + phases[(j - i) % 3]) / 3
+             for j in range(3)] for i in range(3)]
+
+

+    """Exploratory equal-weight iid gaps and passive independent Bernoulli sensors."""
+    n = len(gaps)

+    mats = [transition_matrix(t) for t in gaps]
+    M = [[sum(mat[i][j] for mat in mats) / n for j in range(3)]
+         for i in range(3)]
+    future = [sum(M[i][j] * endpoint[j] for j in range(3)) for i in range(3)]
+    past = [sum(M[j][i] * endpoint[j] for j in range(3)) for i in range(3)]
+    p_center = sum(center) / 3
+    r = sum(center[i] * future[i] for i in range(3)) / (3 * p_center)
+    r_past = sum(center[i] * past[i] for i in range(3)) / (3 * p_center)

+    joint = sum(center[i] * past[i] * future[i] for i in range(3)) / (3 * p_center)

+"""Independent matrix-exponential check for the geometric path audit.
+
+Requires mpmath. This is numerical cross-validation, not the proof.
+"""
+
+import mpmath as mp
+
+
+mp.mp.dps = 60
+q = mp.mpf(1) / 20
+s = 1 + q
+t = mp.mpf(3) / 10
+pi = mp.mpf(1) / 3
+Q = mp.matrix([[-s, 1, q], [q, -s, 1], [1, q, -s]])
+G = mp.matrix([
+    [-s, mp.sqrt(q), mp.sqrt(q)],
+    [mp.sqrt(q), -s, mp.sqrt(q)],
+    [mp.sqrt(q), mp.sqrt(q), -s],
+])
+B = mp.matrix([0, 1, 1])
+P = mp.expm(t * Q)
+a = mp.fsum(pi * P[i, j] for i in (1, 2) for j in (1, 2)) / (mp.mpf(2) / 3)
+f = B - mp.matrix([a, a, a])
+v = mp.expm(t * G) * f
+e_nu_w = pi * (v[1] ** 2 + v[2] ** 2)
+e_q_w = mp.fsum(
+    pi * P[j, i] * P[i, k] * (B[j] - a) * (B[k] - a)
+    for i in (1, 2) for j in range(3) for k in range(3)
+)
+affinity = mp.exp(-2 * t * (s - 2 * mp.sqrt(q)))
+print("a", mp.nstr(a, 50))
+print("E_Q W", mp.nstr(e_q_w, 50))
+print("E_nu W", mp.nstr(e_nu_w, 50))
+print("affinity", mp.nstr(affinity, 50))
+print("lost mass times score minimum", mp.nstr(a * (1 - a) * (1 - affinity), 50))
+assert e_q_w < 0 < e_nu_w
+assert -e_q_w < a * (1 - a) * (1 - affinity)

+# S12 follow-up — what dry conductance can certify about a repaired metallic strut
+
+**Status, 15 October 2026:** Exact conditional derivation and counterexamples. No strut was fabricated, plated, measured, or mechanically tested here. The result concerns **small-signal axial stiffness**, not tensile strength, toughness, fatigue life, or repair novelty.
+
+## Direct answer
+
+**Yes, under a one-dimensional shared-path model:** for a straight axial strut with any unknown positive cross-section \(A(x)\), if every load-bearing and electronically conducting segment has local \(E(x)/\sigma(x)\ge m>0\), the bulk axial stiffness obeys \(k_b\ge m g_b\). The shape and local plating thickness need not be reconstructed. **No, for an arbitrary three-dimensional conductive repair or arbitrary contacts:** a conductive path can bend, slip, run around the load path, or terminate in an electrically good but mechanically unbonded interface. Dry terminal conductance alone cannot rule those out. A wet electrochemical current is still further from a structural certificate because electrolyte can provide an ionic path.
+
+## Exact one-dimensional proof and cross-section scope
+
+For a uniform axial force and Ohmic current along a continuous straight strut of length \(L\), let \(B(x)=E(x)A(x)\) be its local axial rigidity and \(S(x)=\sigma(x)A(x)\) its local electronic line conductivity. With ideal end contacts,
+
+\[
+C_b:=k_b^{-1}=\int_0^L\frac{dx}{B(x)},\qquad
+R_b:=g_b^{-1}=\int_0^L\frac{dx}{S(x)}.
+\]
+
+If \(B(x)\ge m S(x)\) almost everywhere, then \(C_b\le R_b/m\), hence
+
+\[
+\boxed{k_b\ge m g_b.}\tag{1}
+\]
+
+For a single metal whose current-carrying section is exactly the strain-carrying section, \(B/S=E/\sigma\); arbitrary changes in the unknown positive \(A(x)\) cancel. For a **bonded, co-strained composite deposit**, \(B=\sum_j E_jA_j\) and \(S=\sum_j\sigma_jA_j\); the same conclusion holds if every included constituent has \(E_j/\sigma_j\ge m\). This includes unknown local thickening only when every electrically counted deposit actually shares axial load. A conductive coating that slips on the parent metal contributes to \(S\) but not to \(B\), so the premise fails.
+
+The word “arbitrary” above means arbitrary **axial cross-section profile within the 1D model**. It does not cover a winding 3D filament. For a slender U- or S-shaped wire, terminal separation in the service direction can be taken up mainly by bending. Electrical conductance scales as \(\sigma A/L\), while bending stiffness scales as \(EI/L^3\); their ratio is of order \((E/\sigma)(I/(AL^2))\), arbitrarily smaller than \(E/\sigma\) for a thin wire. A manufactured straight guide or post-repair imaging/assay must exclude such bypass geometry before using (1).
+
+## Both contacts: exact sufficient condition and a usable weaker bound
+
+Let the two terminal interfaces have **electrical series resistances** \(r_L,r_R\ge0\) and **axial mechanical series compliances** \(c_L,c_R\ge0\) on the service branch. Let \(r_{\rm lead}\ge0\) be lead resistance. Suppose there is no parallel electrical leakage or second structural load path. Then the measured dry two-terminal conductance and joined stiffness are
+
+\[
+G=\frac{1}{R_b+r_L+r_R+r_{\rm lead}},\qquad
+k=\frac{1}{C_b+c_L+c_R}.
+\]
+
+A **sufficient aggregate condition on both contacts** is
+
+\[
+\boxed{c_L+c_R\le (r_L+r_R)/m.}\tag{2}
+\]
+
+The stronger, individually checkable conditions \(c_L\le r_L/m\) and \(c_R\le r_R/m\) also suffice. Combining (1) and (2) gives \(C_b+c_L+c_R\le(R_b+r_L+r_R)/m\le 1/(mG)\), and therefore
+
+\[
+\boxed{k\ge mG.}\tag{3}
+\]
+
+Condition (2) is not a law of metal contacts. If the bulk achieves only the lower material ratio \(E/\sigma=m\), it is the exact worst-case aggregate condition for (3) when lead resistance is ignored. Extra *electrical* series resistance by itself only lowers \(G\), making a lower stiffness bound more conservative; uncontrolled *mechanical* contact compliance destroys the inference. A bonded contact could have very low electrical resistance and nonzero compliance, so (2) may be too strong to certify in practice.
+
+A more usable interface contract is an independently measured upper bound \(c_L+c_R\le c^{+}\). It yields, without knowing the individual electrical contact resistances,
+
+\[
+\boxed{k\ge\left[\frac{1}{mG}+c^{+}\right]^{-1}
+=\frac{mG}{1+mGc^{+}}.}\tag{4}
+\]
+
+With conservative lower endpoints \(m^{-},G^{-}\), a target \(k\ge k_{\rm req}\) is certified if
+
+\[
+\frac{1}{m^{-}G^{-}}+c^{+}\le \frac{1}{k_{\rm req}}.
+\tag{5}
+\]
+
+The contact-compliance bound must hold for **both ends**, in the actual load direction and over the stated force, time, and temperature envelope. If it is unavailable, no positive lower bound on joined stiffness follows from \(G\), however large the conductance becomes. Four-wire sensing can remove conservative lead resistance but cannot establish mechanical bonding. If an upper bound \(g_{\rm leak}^{+}\) on nonstructural dry shunt conductance is acquired, replace \(G^{-}\) by \(\max\{0,G_{\rm measured}^{-}-g_{\rm leak}^{+}\}\) only after verifying the parallel-circuit decomposition. An unbounded shunt leaves no useful certificate.
+
+## Exact falsifiers: contacts, liquid, and strength
+
+1. **Good electrical contact, failed mechanical contact.** In normalized units take \(R_b=C_b=m=1\), \(r_L=r_R=0\), \(c_L=1,c_R=0\). Then \(G=1\) but \(k=1/2<mG=1\). More sharply, a plated metal filament merely touching one pad can carry a dry low-bias current under compression while the joint has zero tensile stiffness after it separates. Both cases satisfy the bulk material condition and fail only at the interface. A high conductance endpoint would falsely accept the tensile repair.
+2. **Wet ionic shunt.** With no metallic bridge at all, let electrolyte between electrodes have ionic conductance \(G_{\rm ion}>0\). A wet two-terminal current reports \(G_{\rm wet}=G_{\rm ion}\), while axial strut stiffness is zero. Faradaic current and polarization make the relation to metallic conductance still less direct. Measure the electronic low-bias response after rinsing/drying, or validate an independent decomposition; electrochemical plating current is not the \(G\) in (3)–(5). Dry metallic redeposition outside the load path is another possible shunt.
+3. **High stiffness, arbitrarily low strength even with perfect contacts.** Set \(L=1\), \(E=\sigma=m=1\), and \(A(x)=1\) except for a notch of length \(\delta^2\) and area \(\delta^2\). Then \(R_b=C_b=2-\delta^2\), so \(G=k=(2-\delta^2)^{-1}\to1/2\). If local yield stress is bounded by \(Y\), the tensile force capacity at the notch is at most \(Y\delta^2\to0\). Thus even an exactly valid stiffness-conductance certificate says nothing about required proof load under unrestricted fine geometry. A minimum bottleneck length/shape bound, a lower yield or interface-strength bound, and a failure test are additional acquisitions.
+
+## Implication for the proposed repair operation
+
+Bounded geometry that retains the intended routing, electrochemical initiation at a gap, and subsequent chemical thickening are a plausible **process contract**, but they do not establish the assumptions above. The first electronic bridge can be a narrow dendrite, a weakly attached film, or a shunt. Later deposition can raise \(G\) while leaving an oxide-bearing weak interface or a short fine notch. Qualify the actual deposit's \(E/\sigma\) lower envelope, two interface compliances, electronic path exclusivity, and axial geometry before treating a dry \(G\) threshold as a stiffness certificate. Even if all pass, use a direct proof-load and displacement assay for a strength-bearing repair. A destructive shear/tensile sample from the same lot helps characterize the process but cannot replace a task-specific proof test when hidden device-to-device defects matter.

+The strongest equally informed comparator already grows metal at fractures, controls deposited volume/geometry, and directly assays mechanical strength. [US 4,994,154](https://patents.justia.com/patent/4994154) already describes one electrochemical step to establish electrical continuity and a second to thicken the copper bridge. These are direct prior-art barriers to a novelty claim for initiation-plus-thickening or mere conductance feedback. No evidence here shows the proposed certificate beats direct force acceptance after charging bath preparation, coating, rinse/dry, calibration, electrical measurement, proof loading, failed repairs, and lifetime validation.
+
+**Decisive test:** on geometry-controlled struts, deliberately vary interfacial oxide/adhesion and introduce subresolution notches while matching dry terminal \(G\). Blind-predict small-signal axial stiffness using (4), then measure both stiffness and tensile proof-load survival. Include a disconnected strut immersed in plating bath and a nonstructural metallic shunt. If the contact/geometry-validated bound survives but strength at a fixed \(G\) varies, retain the scoped stiffness result and require the direct force assay. If even stiffness violates (4), the claimed material/contact interface was not acquired. No novelty or operational advantage is established by the current derivation.

+# S12 — A conductive load-path certificate for sacrificial release
+
+**Status (15 October 2026):** Original conditional mathematical design and a physically specified, unbuilt MEMS experiment. No device was fabricated or tested here. No release yield, advantage, or new physical effect has been measured. Novelty **UNKNOWN**. The exact benefit over the strongest equally informed incumbent is also **UNKNOWN**.
+
+## Proposed operation and why the substrate matters
+
+Manufacture an array of flexure-supported micromechanical shutters or resonator islands. The permanent flexures hold each island after fabrication. During handling, extra narrow **copper braces** temporarily tie the island to a separate frame bus, protecting the compliant element. Each brace is both an unwanted mechanical constraint and an electrical path from the island electrode to that bus. The permanent sense lead runs along a protected flexure and is electrically isolated from the brace bus. Copper is removed by a qualified selective wet etch; after a rinse and dry, measure island-to-bus conductance and a calibrated service-mode displacement. The target is a specified force–displacement response of the released island, not total identification of the etching chemistry or microscopic defect map.
+
+This uses an unusual coupling manufactured into the object: every *temporary load path* is intended to be an *electrical path*. Under a material contract, the amount of extra mechanical stiffness that can remain is upper-bounded by the electrical conductance of the actual braces. The etch rate, front shape, diffusion geometry, and particular sequence of brace removals can remain hidden. The substrate turns an unknown interior state into a measured task bound; it does not make arbitrary hidden states harmless.
+
+The proposed stack is an insulating substrate, a patterned permanent suspended element/flexures with a protected electrode, exposed copper brace **necks**, and an etch-protected isolated frame bus. Only the necks should be exposed to the release bath; loss of the bus or its contacts before loss of the necks would create a false endpoint. This is a **fabrication proposal**, not a demonstrated stack. Selective copper release in MEMS and a flexure-motion endpoint are experimentally established in the cited Ni–Fe work, but that paper did not build this particular parallel-brace device or validate the electromechanical bound below. Wet processing requires a rinse/dry protocol that does not cause stiction or corrosion. The first demonstration should use large enough structures that individual braces and motion can be independently inspected before attempting dense arrays.
+
+## Exact mathematical mechanism (original derivation)
+
+Take one intended small-displacement service coordinate \(q\). Let the permanent device's service-mode stiffness be \(K_0\). Brace \(i\) has axial displacement \(\alpha_iq\), length \(L_i\), and possibly uneven remaining cross-section \(A_i(x)>0\). On a linear axial branch, with local Young modulus \(E_i(x)>0\) and electrical conductivity \(\sigma_i(x)>0\), its stiffness and dry electrical conductance are
+
+\[
+k_i=\left[\int_0^{L_i}\frac{dx}{E_i(x)A_i(x)}\right]^{-1},\qquad
+g_i=\left[\int_0^{L_i}\frac{dx}{\sigma_i(x)A_i(x)}\right]^{-1}.
+\]
+
+Suppose the qualified material state envelope establishes \(E_i(x)/\sigma_i(x)\le M\) at every point of each residual brace. Then
+
+\[
+\int\frac{dx}{E_iA_i}
+=\int\frac{\sigma_i}{E_i}\frac{dx}{\sigma_iA_i}
+\ge \frac{1}{M}\int\frac{dx}{\sigma_iA_i},
+\quad\text{so}\quad k_i\le M g_i.
+\]
+
+With braces in electrical parallel between the island and brace bus, \(G=\sum_i g_i\). The added stiffness is therefore
+
+\[
+\Delta K=\sum_i\alpha_i^2 k_i
+\le M\sum_i\alpha_i^2g_i
+\le M\alpha_{\max}^2G.\tag{1}
+\]
+
+This survives an unknown nonuniform etch profile: the whole profile enters only through the measured \(G\) and the acquired upper bound \(M\). For uniform rods the result is equality when \(E/\sigma=M\). At an actual physical break, both mechanical and electronic contribution must vanish for the coupling to continue to hold. A false electrical break at a mechanically intact interface invalidates it.
+
+Choose an allowable service stiffness \(K_{\mathrm{lim}}\) and establish an upper bound \(K_0^{+}\) for the permanent flexures, including fabrication scatter. If the dry conductance's conservative upper confidence/uncertainty endpoint \(G^{+}\) satisfies
+
+\[
+K_0^{+}+M\alpha_{\max}^2G^{+}\le K_{\mathrm{lim}},\tag{2}
+\]
+
+then the axial-brace model certifies adequate service compliance without imaging the hidden brace residues. This is a **task threshold**, stronger than the vague instruction to etch until an open-circuit reading. It also permits a small amount of harmless residual copper. If the goal instead requires literal absence of all copper, equation (2) is insufficient.
+
+As copper is physically removed, each edge's conductance falls when its geometry shrinks with fixed conductivity, so the parallel \(G\) falls monotonically. This is the simple form of Rayleigh monotonicity. It justifies pulse/check/continue control without a kinetic model *inside the qualified envelope*. In a real bath, deposition, contact chemistry, ionic shunts, and changes in conductivity can break the observed monotonicity; a monotonic trace is a check, not proof of the envelope.
+
+**Electrical readout detail.** A two-terminal measurement includes series lead and contact resistance. If it is naively used as \(G\), it can understate brace conductance and falsely certify (2). Use Kelvin taps at the island and brace-bus boundaries where possible, and qualify an upper bound on all remaining contact contributions. If only total resistance \(R_{\rm tot}\) is available and the series contribution is known to lie below \(R_s^{+}\), a safe brace-conductance upper bound is \(G^{+}\le 1/(R_{\rm tot}^{-}-R_s^{+})\) only when the denominator is positive and no hidden series interface lies inside the brace path. An ionic wet shunt would usually make the apparent conductance too high, but electrode polarization and contact effects can go either way. Dry measurements or a demonstrated de-embedding procedure are necessary.
+
+## Explicit hidden-state counterexample and substantive redesign
+
+World A has all copper braces severed. World B retains one mechanically intact brace of stiffness \(k=1\) in normalized units, while a thin insulating oxide at its island contact or a broken sense metallization makes its measured conductance \(g=0\). Both worlds return the same open-circuit endpoint and can have the same prior conductance trajectory if the contact degrades at the apparent release time. Yet their service stiffness differs by one unit. Equivalently, an insulating polymer residue can mechanically bridge island and frame after the conductive copper has dissolved. In this world \(E/\sigma\) is unbounded on a load-bearing path, so the hypothesis of (1) fails. The patent cited below independently describes a related problem: mechanically anchoring sacrificial residues can remain after electrical shorts have disappeared.

First, manufacture the *actual* temporary braces as the conductance network, rather than relying on a neighboring release coupon whose local etch may differ. Place no uninstrumented temporary support outside that pattern. Second, after electrical acceptance, apply a predeclared force/field sweep through the intended service mode and measure displacement, hysteresis, and return on the *same device*. The direct motion check is the final functional certificate for the tested force, frequency, temperature, and time envelope. It catches the insulating mechanical bridge even when (2) appears to pass. A viscoelastic bridge that yields during one short sweep and recovers later remains a counterexample to an extrapolated lifetime guarantee; extend the test envelope or retain that risk. The conductance bound's possible benefit is earlier/cheaper determination of when to attempt the functional check, and a quantitative limit on residual brace stiffness. No superiority is claimed until measured against the comparators below.
+
+## Strongest equally informed comparison
+
+The incumbent is not blind fixed-time etching. Give it the same substrate layout, bath, process history, electrical pads, optical access, calibration coupons, and final motion assay. It can use (a) the same actual-device electrical reading, (b) a same-wafer electrical test structure, (c) optical backside or pointer motion monitoring where geometry allows, and (d) direct force–displacement acceptance. Existing electrical sacrificial-layer test structures and direct motion endpoint checks are real prior methods. With the same acquired \(M\) and pads, the incumbent can use inequality (1) too. There is no information-theoretic or demonstrated full-resource advantage over this comparator.
+
+The specific distinction to test is whether putting **all removable service load paths in parallel between two isolated electrodes** reduces missed tethering or unnecessary etch compared with a witness coupon or endpoint-by-time, at acceptable added fabrication/readout cost. A comparator with the same actual-device sensing may tie. A direct functional assay may make the electrical bound redundant. The experiment must report that possibility rather than compare only to an intentionally weak fixed-time recipe.
+
+## Acquisition, preparation, control, reliability, and scale
+
+The operation has to acquire, not assume: (i) the as-built map that all temporary load paths are in the sensed brace network; (ii) conservative \(M\) over partial etch, oxidation, cracks, and contacts; (iii) \(K_0^{+}\) and geometry factors \(\alpha_i\); (iv) bath selectivity for the exact device stack and maximum safe exposure; (v) meter noise floor, leakage, lead/contact resistance, and dry-state reproducibility; and (vi) force/displacement assay calibration. Same-stack destructive coupons with deliberately thinned braces are a practical way to challenge the \(E/\sigma\) bound, but a finite sample only qualifies a stated manufacturing envelope. The final motion test is indispensable if that envelope is not comprehensive.

Process costs include copper etchant, bath preparation and refresh, rinse, critical-point or equivalent anti-stiction dry where required, waste handling, process time, and any extra etch/check cycles. Measurement costs include a low-leakage conductance meter, force or magnetic/electrostatic drive, optical displacement readout, calibration coupons, and rejected devices. The tested copper chemistry's reagent amounts and minutes are literature data, not measurements for this proposed stack. Anodic etching adds electrical work, counterelectrode/control hardware, and a precipitation/passivation hazard; it is an optional comparator, not free acceleration.
+
+For \(N\) devices, measuring each island separately costs at least \(N\) endpoint decisions and usually \(N\) motion checks; multiplexers add leakage and switching time. A wafer-summed conductance can certify a sum only under the same material contract and a much tighter aggregate noise floor. If each device has probability at most \(p\) of an unqualified hidden bypass, the chance of at least one such bypass is at most \(Np\) by a union bound; no value of \(p\) has been measured. Processing yield and lifetime cannot be inferred from one accepted device.
+
+## Primary-source inspection and prior-art boundary
+
+1. [Selby and Shannon, *Anodic Sacrificial Layer Etch (ASLE) for Large Area and Blind Cavity Release of Metallic Structures* (Hilton Head 1998)](https://transducer-research-foundation.org/technical_digests/HiltonHead_1998/hh1998_0252.pdf). **Inspected:** abstract, Cu/Ni experimental stack and comparison, results discussing etch-front rates, Cu precipitation, passivation and bubble limits. +# Odd-parity lift of a single-reset renewal process
+
+**Status (15 October 2026):** self-contained analytic construction and exact rational check, with **novelty unknown and probably limited by older generalized-detailed-balance work**. The construction is a precise boundary on what a two-label waiting-time law can establish when microscopic time-reversal parity is left unspecified. It is neither a claim of free physical operation nor a contradiction of the existing even-variable result.
+
+## The exact operation
+
+Take any finite irreducible continuous-time Markov generator \(Q\) on \(\{a\}\cup B\), with \(a\) the *only* state observed as \(A\) and every state of \(B\) observed as \(B\). Let its strictly positive stationary row vector be \(\pi=(\pi_a,\pi_B)\). Write
+
+\[
+Q=\begin{pmatrix}-\lambda&\lambda\alpha\\t&S\end{pmatrix},\qquad
+\lambda>0,\quad\alpha\mathbf1=1,\quad t=-S\mathbf1.
+\]
+
+The visible process is an alternating renewal process: an \(A\) dwell is exponential with rate \(\lambda\); the density of the following complete \(B\) dwell is
+
+\[
+f_B(u)=\alpha e^{Su}t. \tag{1}
+\]
+
+At every return to the singleton \(a\), the strong Markov property resets the cycle. Irreducibility makes \(S\) transient, so (1) is a probability density with finite mean.
+
+Let \(Q^\dagger\) be the stationary time reversal, \(Q^\dagger_{ij}=\pi_jQ_{ji}/\pi_i\) for \(i\ne j\), with the same diagonal as \(Q\). Introduce two copies, \(+\) running \(Q\) and \(-\) running \(Q^\dagger\). Add only the two equal-rate transitions
+
+\[
+(a,+)\xrightleftharpoons[\varepsilon]{\varepsilon}(a,-),\qquad\varepsilon>0.
+\]
+
+Observe \((a,\pm)\) as \(A\) and \((i,\pm)\), \(i\in B\), as \(B\). Treat the sign as odd under time reversal: \(\theta(i,+)=(i,-)\), \(\theta(i,-)=(i,+)\). The resulting \(2|Q|\)-state generator \(L\) is irreducible, exactly reproduces the **entire stationary visible path law** of \(Q\), and its stationary path law is invariant under \(x(u)\mapsto\theta x(T-u)\) for every \(T\). Thus its path-space relative entropy against this parity-reversed path law is exactly zero on every finite interval.
+
+This is an all-dimension statement for the single-reset class. It does not require the \(B\) phase representation to be minimal, diagonalizable, or bidirectionally supported. It does require exact stationarity, a genuine singleton reset, the specified parity assignment, exact reverse rates, and positive \(\varepsilon\).
+
+## Proof of exact dwell and path-law preservation
+
+Put \(D=\operatorname{diag}(\pi_B)\). Stationarity gives \(\pi_Bt=\pi_a\lambda\). Directly from the definition of \(Q^\dagger\), its \(B\) killed block, normalized entrance row, and exit column are
+
+\[
+S^\dagger=D^{-1}S^{\mathsf T}D,\qquad
+\alpha^\dagger=\frac{t^{\mathsf T}D}{\pi_a\lambda},\qquad
+t^\dagger=\pi_a\lambda D^{-1}\alpha^{\mathsf T}. \tag{2}
+\]
+
+The reverse \(A\) exit rate is \(\lambda\), because the diagonals of \(Q\) and \(Q^\dagger\) coincide; \(\alpha^\dagger\mathbf1=1\) by stationarity. Similarity of the killed semigroups gives the identity, for **every** \(u\ge0\),
+
+\[
+\begin{aligned}
+\alpha^\dagger e^{S^\dagger u}t^\dagger
+&=t^{\mathsf T}D( D^{-1}e^{S^{\mathsf T}u}D )D^{-1}\alpha^{\mathsf T}\\
+&=t^{\mathsf T}e^{S^{\mathsf T}u}\alpha^{\mathsf T}
+=\alpha e^{Su}t.
+\end{aligned}\tag{3}
+\]
+
+Thus a \(B\) excursion has the same complete-duration law in either orientation. While in either \(A\) state, the rate of a *visible* exit to \(B\) is \(\lambda\), independent of the sign, even though hidden sign flips occur at rate \(\varepsilon\). Conditional on the entire visible and hidden past at an entrance to \(A\), the next \(A\) duration is therefore \(\mathrm{Exp}(\lambda)\). The sign selected at the subsequent visible exit may depend on that duration, but (3) makes the conditional \(B\) duration distribution independent of that sign. Hence the pair of successive \(A,B\) durations has the same product law \(\mathrm{Exp}(\lambda)\otimes f_B\) conditional on every prior cycle. Induction gives the same iid cycle sequence as \(Q\). Its unique stationary time placement is determined by the cycle-length bias, so the stationary visible càdlàg path laws, not merely marginal waiting-time histograms, agree.
+
+The stationary law of the lift is \(\rho_{i,+}=\rho_{i,-}=\pi_i/2\). Within each copy stationarity follows from \(\pi Q=\pi Q^\dagger=0\); the two reset flips balance. Irreducibility follows because each copy is irreducible and the reset flips connect them. For any within-copy edge, the defining identity of \(Q^\dagger\) yields
+
+\[
+\rho_xL_{xy}=\rho_{\theta y}L_{\theta y,\theta x}. \tag{4}
+\]
+
+For either reset flip, (4) holds directly. Also \(\rho_x=\rho_{\theta x}\) and \(L_{xx}=L_{\theta x,\theta x}\), including at \(a\), where both diagonals gain \(-\varepsilon\). Multiplying (4) along a finite jump path, with the holding-time factors and initial stationary mass, proves equality of the forward path density and its parity-reversed density. Therefore the parity path KL is \(0\) for every \(T\), including on edges that were one-way in \(Q\). This is a statement about a specified path involution. It does not assert that ordinary even-variable entropy production vanishes.
+
+## Exact non-Markov example and executed check
+
+For the ring family used in [Aznagulov's preprint, §8.5 and §8.8](https://arxiv.org/html/2609.14623), choose clockwise rate \(1\), counterclockwise rate \(q\in(0,1)\), and \(a=0\):
+
+\[
+Q_q=\begin{pmatrix}-(1+q)&1&q\\q&-(1+q)&1\\1&q&-(1+q)\end{pmatrix},\quad
+\pi=(1/3,1/3,1/3).
+\]
+
+Writing \(s=1+q\), its \(B\) representation is \(\alpha=(1,q)/s\), \(S=\left(\begin{smallmatrix}-s&1\\q&-s\end{smallmatrix}\right)\), \(t=(q,1)^{\mathsf T}\). Direct matrix inversion gives
+
+\[
+\widehat f_B(z)=\frac{(2q/s)z+(1+q+q^2)}{z^2+2sz+(1+q+q^2)}. \tag{5}
+\]
+
+At \(q=1/20\), \(f_B(0)=2/21\) and \(f'_B(0)=341/400>0\). Let \(g(u)=\Pr\{\text{the entered }B\text{ dwell exceeds }u\}\). Then \(g'(0)=-2/21\), \(g''(0)=-341/400\), and for all sufficiently small \(h>0\),
+
+\[
+g(2h)-g(h)^2
+=-\left(\frac{341}{400}+\frac4{441}\right)h^2+O(h^3)<0. \tag{6}
+\]
+
+Equation (6) is a concrete visible path event: after the process has survived \(h\) in \(B\), its chance of surviving another \(h\) is lower than it was on entering \(B\). A two-state time-homogeneous Markov process would have equality by exponential memorylessness. Both the original ring and the six-state parity lift generate the same strict inequality. Thus the lift preserves a genuinely non-Markov observation, not just a two-point statistic.
+
+The file [verify_odd_lift.py](verify_odd_lift.py) uses Python Fraction arithmetic for \(q=1/20\), \(\varepsilon=1/7\). Its saved [output](verify_odd_lift.json) verifies row sums, stationarity, parity-paired holding rates and all 30 off-diagonal parity-balance identities, plus equality of the first nine \(B\)-density Taylor coefficients. These finite checks are reproducibility support; equations (2)–(4) are the proof for arbitrary finite dimension.
+
+The original ring and the lifted model have the same **ordinary** entropy-production rate, \((1-q)\log(1/q)=(19/20)\log20\approx2.84594566\) at \(q=1/20\). The two half-weight branches each contribute half of the original cost, and the reset flips contribute none to ordinary edge cost. The lift's extra stationary microscopic jump activity is \(\varepsilon\pi_a=1/21\), in addition to the ring's \(s=21/20\). The flip rate can tend to zero, but the sign-mixing time then diverges; \(\varepsilon=0\) is a reducible stationary mixture and does not meet the theorem's irreducibility assumption.
+
+## Comparator, prior art, and physical boundary
+
+The strongest equally informed simple competitor is the original three-state ring itself: it exactly produces the whole renewal law with half the states and no parity-register control. The six-state lift changes the *definition of microscopic reversal*, not the visible task or the ordinary cost. A [3 October 2026 unrefereed candidate release](https://www.evidencepress.org/releases/hidden-dissipation-floor/) states an all-dimension positive ordinary/even-reversal lower bound \(V_\infty(P_{1/20})>0.017568198744\) and explicitly excludes odd-variable extensions. Our construction lies outside that reversal convention, so the bound and this exact zero parity-path KL can coexist. The earlier preprint states \(V_\infty(P_{1/20})=0\) only as a conjecture (§6, lines 239–242); the later candidate claims to refute it under its stated even-variable assumptions. Neither item is a laboratory measurement or an externally peer-reviewed validation of this lift.
+
+The broad idea is substantially anticipated. [Barra, Clerc and Tirapegui (1997), *Detailed balance in non-equilibrium systems*](https://doi.org/10.1080/02681119708806236) says in its [author-uploaded abstract](https://www.researchgate.net/publication/245326839_Detailed_balance_in_non-equilibrium_systems) that a stationary Markov process can be put in generalized detailed balance by adding odd parameters. The full paper could not be retrieved here, so its exact construction and whether it contains the single-reset, irreducible, whole-observation-law specialization remain unverified. [Lee, Kwon and Park (2012), equations 3–9 and 19](https://arxiv.org/html/1209.0543) explicitly define parity-flipped path reversal and require both generalized detailed balance and parity-symmetric stationary distribution for equilibrium; (4) and \(\rho_x=\rho_{\theta x}\) satisfy those mathematical requirements. [Skinner and Dunkel (2021), pp. 1–3](https://math.mit.edu/~dunkel/Papers/2021SkDu_PRL.pdf) already use nonmonotone waiting-time densities as ordinary-reversal nonequilibrium evidence. The initial attempt here to derive a dimension-independent ordinary-reversal floor by additive symmetrization was independently reproduced but preempted by the October release's same construction and stronger certified bound. Its novelty is not claimed.
+
+The additional sign must correspond to an actual microscopic odd variable for generalized reversal to have thermodynamic meaning. Naming a hidden bit “odd” is not a physical implementation. A physical realization would have to acquire or calibrate \(\pi\), synthesize the exact reversed rates \(Q^\dagger\), sustain two matched branch architectures, cause sign flips only at the \(A\) reset, and verify the parity of the hidden variable under genuine time reversal. Those preparation, sensing, control, and reliability costs are unmeasured here. A rate mismatch generically breaks (3) or (4). Without a reservoir-resolved local-detailed-balance model, zero parity path KL cannot be promoted to zero energy use or a working device. No experiment was performed.
+
+**Decisive next test:** obtain the full 1997 paper and compare its construction line by line; then demand a concrete physical odd coordinate and reservoir-resolved transition model for the six-state example. If no physically admissible parity assignment realizes (4), the mathematical countermodel remains valid but does not weaken an experimentally grounded dissipation inference. If such an assignment exists, check whole-path observed dwell correlations and measured heat against the exact rates; any disagreement falsifies the proposed physical mapping.

+"""

+from fractions import Fraction as F
+from math import log
+import json
+
+
+def mv(a, v):
+    return [sum(a[i][j] * v[j] for j in range(len(v)))
+            for i in range(len(a))]
+
+
+def dot(u, v):
+    return sum(u[i] * v[i] for i in range(len(u)))
+
+
+def row_stationary(pi, q):
+    return [sum(pi[i] * q[i][j] for i in range(len(pi)))
+            for j in range(len(pi))]
+
+
+q = F(1, 20)
+eps = F(1, 7)
+s = 1 + q
+Q = [
+    [-s, F(1), q],
+    [q, -s, F(1)],
+    [F(1), q, -s],
+]
+pi = [F(1, 3)] * 3
+assert row_stationary(pi, Q) == [0] * 3
+
+# Stationary time-reversed generator.
+Qrev = [[pi[j] * Q[j][i] / pi[i] for j in range(3)]
+        for i in range(3)]
+assert all(Q[i][i] == Qrev[i][i] for i in range(3))
+assert row_stationary(pi, Qrev) == [0] * 3
+
+# The states are (A,+), (B1,+), (B2,+), (A,-), (B1,-), (B2,-).
+L = [[F(0) for _ in range(6)] for _ in range(6)]
+for i in range(3):
+    for j in range(3):
+        L[i][j] = Q[i][j]
+        L[i + 3][j + 3] = Qrev[i][j]
+L[0][0] -= eps
+L[0][3] = eps
+L[3][3] -= eps
+L[3][0] = eps
+rho = [p / 2 for p in pi] * 2
+theta = [3, 4, 5, 0, 1, 2]
+
+assert all(sum(row) == 0 for row in L)
+assert row_stationary(rho, L) == [0] * 6
+assert all(rho[i] == rho[theta[i]] for i in range(6))
+assert all(L[i][i] == L[theta[i]][theta[i]] for i in range(6))
+assert all(rho[i] * L[i][j] == rho[theta[j]] * L[theta[j]][theta[i]]
+           for i in range(6) for j in range(6) if i != j)
+assert all(L[i][j] >= 0 for i in range(6) for j in range(6) if i != j)
+
+reached = {0}
+while True:
+    new = reached | {j for i in reached for j in range(6) if L[i][j] > 0}
+    if new == reached:
+        break
+    reached = new
+assert reached == set(range(6))
+
+# Original and reversed B dwell derivatives: alpha S^k t.
+alpha = [Q[0][1] / s, Q[0][2] / s]
+S = [[Q[i][j] for j in (1, 2)] for i in (1, 2)]
+t = [Q[i][0] for i in (1, 2)]
+alphar = [Qrev[0][1] / s, Qrev[0][2] / s]
+Sr = [[Qrev[i][j] for j in (1, 2)] for i in (1, 2)]

+v, vr = t[:], tr[:]
+derivatives = []

+
+print(json.dumps({
+    "q": str(q),

+# Poison-written local regeneration in a driven Pt electrode array
+
+15 October 2026 (Brisbane). **Status: candidate operation, not a demonstrated invention.** The bare phenomenon—CO-poisoning-induced autonomous oscillation of formic-acid oxidation on Pt under resistive or galvanostatic control—is prior art. The narrower proposed operation is *spatially selective regeneration*: electrically and ionically partition a Pt microelectrode array so that each patch's own adsorbed-CO history controls its cleaning excursion while its neighbors continue producing current. It could matter only if heterogeneity makes common pulses wasteful, and only if its full power, segmentation, control and lifetime costs beat branch-resolved electronics and a poison-resistant catalyst. That has not been shown. The simple resistor implementation fails a useful energy bound below; an individually current-fed version is the substantive redesign left for experiment.
+
+## Exact task and physical memory
+
+The scientific access problem is to keep a flow-fed formic-acid anode productive when local Pt patches acquire different, mostly unobserved adsorbate histories. The desired output is net electrical energy per feed and Pt area over an eight-hour run, with measured CO2 and catalyst retention, not merely current oscillations. The available inputs are a fabricated array, formic-acid/acid electrolyte, a common power/load interface, and each branch's electrical terminals; CO coverage is *not* initially supplied. The array must acquire its own control signal from the reaction. A three-electrode diagnostic can be used during calibration and adjudication, but its reference and spectroscopy are not free components of the deployed controller.
+
+Choose lithographic Pt islands in parallel flow channels, with a counter electrode near each island and individually wired branches. Formic acid has a productive direct pathway and a CO-forming pathway on Pt. Adsorbed CO blocks active sites and persists across moments of the applied drive: coverage \(\theta_j\) is the local memory. A heavily blocked island passes less productive current. Under a local series impedance or an imposed branch current, its interfacial potential rises. At sufficiently positive potential CO oxidizes/desorbs; current recovers and the potential returns to a productive range. **The marking reaction changes the catalyst's rate and the circuit's current; it consumes sites, fuel and charge.** There is no spectator reporter with cost-free, one-way information flow. Other adsorbates, fuel starvation and solution resistance also change current, so the mark is not specific without calibration.
+
+A minimal coupled model for island \(j\) is
+
+\[
+ C_j\dot E_j=I_{\mathrm{feed},j}(E_j,u_j)-I_{\mathrm{prod},j}(E_j,\theta_j,c_j)-I_{\mathrm{strip},j}(E_j,\theta_j),\qquad
+ \dot\theta_j=k_{\mathrm{form},j}(E_j,c_j)(1-\theta_j)^q-k_{\mathrm{strip},j}(E_j)\theta_j.
+\]
+
+Here \(C_j\) includes double-layer and lead capacitance; \(I_{\rm strip}\) is the Faradaic charge of CO removal and must be separated from direct-path current. It may still convert stored fuel carbon to CO2 and contribute electrical output, but at a different interfacial potential after blocking productive sites. For a resistive branch \(I_{\rm feed}=(V_b-E_j)/R_j\), so the written \(\theta_j\) changes the load line. The control-relevant times are \(t_{\rm poison}\), \(t_{\rm strip}\), \(R_j C_j\), flow residence and inter-island ionic coupling. The equations are a **proposal**, not a fit to the cited experiments. In real Pt formic-acid oxidation, water/OH and formate coverages also enter; the one-variable model must be rejected if it cannot predict the measured phase traces and stripping charge.
+
+## A quantitative obstruction for the easiest implementation
+
+Let \(I_p>I_c\) be branch currents just before poisoning and just before cleaning at the same bus voltage, and let the necessary interfacial-potential rise be \(\Delta E=E_c-E_p>0\). The resistor load law gives exactly
+
+\[
+R(I_p-I_c)=\Delta E,\qquad
+\frac{P_{R,p}}{I_p}=R I_p=\frac{\Delta E}{1-I_c/I_p}\geq\Delta E.
+\]
+
+Thus the resistor burns at least \(\Delta E\) joules per productive coulomb, even with nearly zero poisoned current; partial poisoning makes the cost larger. This is a circuit identity, not an empirical no-go for other controllers. For an *illustrative design target* \(E_p=0.55\) and \(E_c=0.75\) V vs RHE, \(I_p=0.20\) and \(I_c=0.02\) microampere, \(R\) must be at least \(1.11\) megohms and the productive-state drop is at least \(0.222\) V. The dissipated energy is at least \(0.222\) J/C, or \(42.9\) kJ per mole of formic acid if two electrons per molecule pass through that branch. The example currents and required threshold gap were **not measured** for a particular chip; the 0.2-V gap is motivated only by the Pt(111) productive/CO-stripping windows below. Chip geometry and electrolyte must establish the actual windows. A shallow current response to \(\theta\) only worsens the bound.
+
+This also explains why a claimed free chemical reporter would be misleading: the useful signal is a finite loss of reaction current, and converting it to a 0.2-V cleaning swing with a passive resistor charges the productive operation continuously. The old two-electrode microchip experiment used a 10-Mohm branch resistor and observed single-electrode oscillations at about 0.53 Hz, but on its stated no-Bi condition the oscillations lasted roughly 2–5 minutes before the electrode fell into a low-current poisoned state. Those circuit voltages are not RHE interfacial voltages and cannot be substituted into the illustrative bound without a measured local potential.
+
+## Redesign: local current-fed cleaning, not a hidden sensor
+
+Replace each continuously dissipative resistor with an individually regulated branch-current feed and a bounded compliance voltage. With \(I_{\rm feed,j}=I_{0j}\), poisoning drives \(E_j\) upward by charging \(C_j\); CO oxidation returns the branch to its lower potential. In a fuel cell this stage must be an efficient, regulated load/power converter; in a driven half-cell it is a current source. Either way, its energy balance is measured at the external bus. The *chemical memory remains* \(\theta_j\), not an electronic estimate of it. The electronic stage is an actuator whose power conversion loss, leakage, compliance headroom and fabrication area must be charged. Total two-terminal voltage does not by itself bound the Pt interfacial potential when cathode polarization and solution resistance drift; a local reference or a validated conservative estimator is needed for a dissolution limit, and its cost belongs to the design. The circuit cannot manufacture information about whether a low current means CO, starvation, OH blocking or a dry channel. A local high-potential probe/strip excursion can make that discrimination after the fact via its measured stripping charge, but the probe consumes charge and changes the surface. A subsequent local refractory interval can be stored in a finite capacitor/latch to prevent repeated fruitless excursions. This added two-timescale memory is a proposed engineering extension, with branch electronics explicitly counted; its novelty remains **UNKNOWN**.
+
+The physical prediction worth testing is limited: when poisoning hazard varies substantially across islands, local regeneration should avoid oxidizing still-clean neighbors, whereas a common waveform exposes every island. This is not an inherent advantage over a branch-resolved controller. If a local event has cleaning energy \(e_i\) and event rate \(\lambda_i\), ideal selective actuation costs \(\sum_i\lambda_i e_i\) per unit time. A common pulse at rate \(f\) costs roughly \(f\sum_i e_i\), but an equally informed branch-resolved electronic controller approaches the same \(\sum_i\lambda_i e_i\), subject to its own sensing/drive cost. The proposed material-circuit coupling earns a capability claim only through measured savings in apparatus, latency, energy, reliability or scale after those costs are included. It does not have an information-theoretic advantage over an equally informed controller.
+
+There is also an exact ambiguity: construct two islands with the same terminal \(I(t),E(t)\) until a trigger time, one blocked by CO and one temporarily starved of HCOOH (or altered by OH/flow). Any controller whose only input is that terminal history must take the same action in both worlds. A cleaning excursion can rescue the first and needlessly oxidize the second. Coupled chemistry may distinguish them *after* a perturbation, but there is no zero-cost pre-trigger inference. This counterexample is independent of a particular kinetic fit.
+
+## Real evidence inspected and what it does (and does not) support
+

Its potential scale and electrolyte must not be silently interchanged with the RHE values above.
+
+The literature search was targeted, not exhaustive. No reported rate in this report is inferred from an article's oscillation frequency. No original wet-lab observation or device simulation was performed. The resistor inequality and terminal-history ambiguity are my derivations; the reported experiments and numerical values above belong to the cited authors.
+
+## Matched comparator and complete-resource contract
+
+The strongest **control** comparator uses the same segmented Pt islands, flow, electrolyte, wiring and per-island power stages, measures each branch's current/potential, and applies optimized local pulses or galvanostatic cycles using the same calibration budget. It may use operando stripping-charge calibration and can reproduce any successful potential history generated by the material coupling. Compare also (i) common optimized pulses on the same Pt array, (ii) no dynamic control, and (iii) Pd-monolayer/Pt or the best measured poison-resistant electrode at equal catalyst area, catalyst mass, preparation and life. An advantageous Pt scheme must beat the best of these under the declared objective; beating common pulses alone is too weak.

A monitored laboratory reference/SEIRAS apparatus is an adjudicator and belongs in acquisition cost if its information is used to tune the deployed scheme. A shared fuel source or imposed current is an energy input, not a free driver.

+Before fabrication, the minimum kinetic contract is a measured branch-resolved \(E,\theta,I\) map with a region where \(\partial I_{\rm prod}/\partial\theta<0\), a reachable strip region with \(k_{\rm strip}\) fast enough to outrun poisoning, and an excursion below the measured dissolution limit.
